subject: Henry (cousin)
statement: Portion of regiment sent to assist Louisianians; Col Burleson a 'Rosin Heel' catcher; joined command in Hopkins County last of Nov; prisoners to Tyler and Shreveport; guns to Bonham; holidays at home 15 days; Crockett; San Augustine; brigade to Hempstead by 10 Feb
verbatim_quotation: In the Last part of the fall a portion of our Regt was sent out to assist the Louisianians in getting into the Service ... Col Burleson having become famous as a "Rosin Heel" catcher ... I joined the Command in Hopkins County the Last of Nov ... Our Brigade is ordered to be at Hempstead Tex by the 10th of Feb

verbatim_quotation: Jim Lowder of Ross' Regt is home on furlough. The Squad he came With brought Some Arms across the "Trans[[illegible]]" [[illegible]] 6 millions in Confed. Money.

subject: James (cousin)

verbatim_quotation: We have not heard from [[illegible]] & James Since the middle of Oct. James was [[illegible]] Wounded [[illegible]] in the Chickamauga Battle. I am very anxious to know how They came off at the Chattanooga fight.

subject: Mrs Claunch murder case
statement: Murder of Mrs Claunch by her daughter under consideration in the Waxahachie court
verbatim_quotation: I have visited Waxahachie twice — a very important case being under Consideration in the Court — To wit; The murder of a Mrs Claunch by her Daughter — The case has not yet been decided but from the evidence I have heard believe she will come clear — but not in the Eyes of the people — as innocent of the offence.

subject: Red Oak Camp Ground

verbatim_quotation: From Waxa on Monday I went to Red Oak Camp Ground — Camp meeting being on hand ... They had Shouting times that night

subject: Henry's command
statement: June 1863 ordered west; 1 Aug to Mississippi Valley near Natchez; 31 Aug brigade started for Arkansas; 'Seen the Elephant in La'; Genl Steele; Majors' Div; Walker's
verbatim_quotation: About The 1st of Aug. We moved to the Miss. Valley near Natchez — remained there a Couple of Weeks & then were ordered to Our former field (Ark). On the 31st of Aug the Brigade Started on their way rejoicing. We had Seen the Elephant in La

subject: Henry's squad
statement: Surprised 28 Aug 1863 at 3 AM; 30 horses lost; Capt [[Vardeman?]]
verbatim_quotation: Whilst Scouting on the Miss Our Squad turned over about 30 fine Horses their arms &c to the Yankee ... They were Completely Surprised at 3 oclk AM on the 28 of Aug

subject: Bob; Jeffie; Lizzie; John; Laura; Mother; Sam Austin
statement: Persons in the Sept 1863 letter
verbatim_quotation: Bob got to Camps the day before I left ... Jeffie was down last week. / We Learn Lizzie spent Sunday with you & she Returned to John on Monday. [[Laura?]] Spent last night here. Mother has had a very Sick Spell is getting over it. ... [[Br?]] Sam Austin Called in today Returning from the meeting

subject: Lafayette and James
statement: Heavy fight 22 July 1863; regiment went in with 320, came out with about 80; James narrow escape
verbatim_quotation: We recently Recd a Letter from Lafayette of [[date?]] 1st of Aug. Their Brigade had a heavy fight on the 22nd of July — their Regt went into Battle with 320 & Came out with about 80 — James who was in the [[illegible]] had a narrow Escape

subject: Hage; Clem

verbatim_quotation: Those of their Co that was not killed had to Surrender & while They were Stacking arms Hage [[illegible]] through [[illegible]] & Clem [[illegible]] was found at hind

subject: Bob (R D G)
statement: Old hunting companion and schoolmate writes from Cold Springs; hunted gobblers on old Brushy; nearly four years since he saw George; weighs 175; Co. F
verbatim_quotation: Cold Springs Texas / Sept 19th /63 ... it has been A long time since we used to meet down on old Brushy and give the old gobblers a round ... nearly Four years have pass Since I Saw you ... I weigh 175 pounds and the largest Devil in co. (F.)

subject: Bob (R D G)
statement: Big meeting in camp, forty mourners
verbatim_quotation: There is a big meeting going on in camp. There was about forty mourners last night. They haven't got me yet

subject: Bob (R D G)

verbatim_quotation: I have not heard from my Brothers East of the miss for Two or three months ... As Ever Your Cousin / R D G ... Bob

subject: James (Tupelo)
statement: Wounded 22 July [1864] charging the enemy's works; left wrist and hand; fever from mid-August; 60 days furlough in October to Mobile; stopped at Demopolis with Mrs Brassfield
verbatim_quotation: Tupelo Mississippi Jan 25th/65 / Dear Brother / As Brother Lafayette will Start home in a few days on furlough ... I was painfully wounded on the 22nd of July while Charging the enemys works The ball Struck me on the the left wrist and passed throw my hand

subject: James (Tupelo)
statement: Federals destroyed railroad; in hospital at Columbus Miss.; hand still running; wrist stiff; brigade about 400 of five regiments; four of old Co I fit for duty; Lafayette 75 days furlough
verbatim_quotation: Thair is very few of our Brigade left only about 4 hundred out of five Regiments / Thair is only four of old Co "I" left that is able for duty. one to evry 7 is furloughed to go to Texas Brother Lafayette gets a 75 days furlough to go home

subject: Squire; the Jetton boys (Jeppe, Billy, Charly); the Six Texas Boys
statement: Named in the Tupelo letter; Jeppe Jetton in prison
verbatim_quotation: Squire gets a furlough ... I have not heard from our cousins (the Jetton boys) lately Jeppe is in prison Billy & Charly were well when last heard from. The Six Texas Boys were all well when last heard from.

subject: Sylvana
statement: Meeting at Sylvana with dinner on the ground; visitors from Ennis, Oak Cliff, Waxahachie
verbatim_quotation: yesterday was a "big" day. According to announcement there was dinner on the ground. And such another dinner. About the finest ever spread at Sylvana. Among visitors present was White Stirman and [[deleted: illegible]] wife ... and Nellie Russell ... From Oak Cliff were three carloads of people, Jeff Barclay ... the wife of J. C. Estes, the preacher, Bro. Stevens, mother wife and sister, Bro. Melton and family and Bro. Holsenback, and wife. ... Mrs. Dr. Mitchell and family, and Bro. Dunn's family were out from Waxahachie.

subject: White Stirman

verbatim_quotation: White and family going to move right away to Marlin, where White has a job of running a "Watkins" Medicine wagon.

subject: Lucile; Larkin; Kate

verbatim_quotation: No change to report in Lucile's condition ... Larkin is much worse; the disease taking a malignant form day before yesterday ... At Kate's. I found Lucile not so well as last Sunday

subject: Ellis County cotton crop
statement: Crop a failure on 11 August (year not given); worms destroyed bolls
verbatim_quotation: The Ellis Co. cotton crop is a failure today the eleventh of August. The worms have completely destroyed all the bolls and squares, and blooms are scarcer than I ever saw

subject: Ila Duncan; Mayfaire; Bros Duncan
statement: Confessions and baptisms at the meeting
verbatim_quotation: Ila Duncan and Mayfaire made the confession and will be baptized this evening — meeting will close tomorrow night. / Came up today and had a real civilized dinner with [[Bros?]] Duncan.

subject: Red Oak
statement: Old wooden centre of Red Oak burned
verbatim_quotation: Jesse Ligon and family have returned to Red Oak, bag and baggage. ... Did I tell you that the old wooden center of Red Oak burned out from brick to brick? Well the old rat traps are gone. Some loss heavily —

subject: G. D. (George Douglas) to Zella
statement: Signs 'Affectionately G. D.'; 'My peach preserves were highly praised'
verbatim_quotation: Affectionately G. D. / Do the best you can for yourself while you are there. Dont bother about me. / My peach preserves were highly praised

subject: Clarence & Kate; Sid Farrar; Glenn; Roland
statement: Stayed with Clarence & Kate; puncture fixed at Rockett with Sid Farrar; Kate's children look bad; Roland's house in the pasture
verbatim_quotation: I staid with Clarence & Kate Sunday night ... so I drove to Rockett on the rim, and with the help of Sid Farrar soon had it righted up. ... Glenn was not well ... Will likely come to Roland's house in the pasture.

subject: Aunt Nannie; Ruth; Elmer Carter; Edwina
statement: Letter from Paris forwarded; Aunt Nannie; Ruth's plum jelly; Elmer Carter takes the cow; Edwina's letter
verbatim_quotation: The letter to you from Paris I opened ... Will send yours to your Aunt Nannie ... Ruth gave me a glass of plum jelly ... Elmer Carter is very glad to get all of the Cow. ... Tell Edwina I enjoyed reading her good letter hugely.

subject: Ed
statement: Zella staying where Ed's expenses are enormous
verbatim_quotation: I know Ed's expenses must be enormous; but be sure you do not add any to them.

subject: G. D.'s housekeepers
statement: Housekeepers left for Bartlett, Texas; George 'baching'
verbatim_quotation: Our house keepers packed up their goods Saturday, and Sunday Evening loaded them on two wagons, and Monday morning pulled out for Bartlett Texas. ... So my prospects for baching grows brighter from day to day. ... My nieces cant understand why I persist in staying at home

subject: Feterita patch
statement: Hens water below the feterita patch
verbatim_quotation: They mainly water just below the Feterita patch at a swamp spring, and the feterita furnishes them fine picking.

subject: Olaf; Bro. Duncan; Bro. Dunn; Dr. Stoker
statement: Olaf wished to be baptized; Dr. Stoker gave him a few days to live
verbatim_quotation: Word came down last night that Olaf wished to be baptized, so Bro. Duncan returned immediately to Red Oak to make preparation ... Dr. Stoker told the friends that apparently he had only a few days to live. This is hard on Kate but not unexpected.

subject: Olaf
statement: Died at six thirty on a Wednesday evening; buried at the Rawlins cemetery; Bro Dunn spoke at the tabernacle
verbatim_quotation: Olaf died yesterday evening at six thirty. ... Just back from Olof's burial at the Rawlins cemetery — Many friends and sympathizers were present. Bro Dunn made a good comforting talk at the tabernacle.

subject: Larkin

verbatim_quotation: Larkin is sick with blood poisoning. ... To begin with a hen scratched him on the thumb some days ago

subject: Mrs. Wadley

Douglas 80 acre tract, described in Vol. Z, Page 58 of the Deed Records of said County, and the N.E. corner of the J.H. Hedrick 20 acres described in Vol. 179, Page 362 ... Thence S. 30 E., 587 vrs. to the center of Brushy Creek.

subject: Papa (George Douglas) to Zella
statement: Letter from Union City (California postmark) about cancer treatment; wants $100 for the Ford; sell young cattle; note at Waxahachie bank due 11 Sept
verbatim_quotation: Union City Sept 3 — 1923 / My Dear Child — ... I want a hundred dollars for the Ford. No trade. ... Sell the young cattle as it wont pay to winter them. Put up feed for one cow only. Pay the taxes, and have Ligon to attend to note due the / Waxahachie Bank, due the Eleventh of September.

subject: Papa
statement: A large lump came out through his cheek; fears more metastases; radium scattered the trouble; 'This last will be four'
verbatim_quotation: A large lump came out through my cheek, and there is another to follow not so large. ... The thing I fear is that more Metastases may set up — / The radium had scattered the trouble into my cheek ... This last will be four that has been caught up with

subject: Papa
statement: Trip would cost $100; wants all debts at home paid
verbatim_quotation: You may have to come out here; and it will take a hundred dollars to cover the trip; and I want all debts at home paid so as to know how best to do.

subject: Papa
statement: Cannot come back by Nashville because of the altitude over the Cumberland Mountains; Anna's visit
verbatim_quotation: No! I cant come back by Nashville. I would not risk the altitude over the Cumberland Mountains. I am glad Anna stopped to see you.

subject: Papa
statement: 'you are all I have that is best to live for'; car cranking days over
verbatim_quotation: I would love for you to be here, for I get very blue and lonesome at times, and you are all I have that is best to live for. With the number of my years I cant stay here long ... my car cranking days are over.

subject: Allie; Dr Bird
statement: Allie leaves to run a dormitory; George staying with Dr Bird
verbatim_quotation: Allie leaves tomorrow for [[illegible]] to run a Dormitory. I am staying with Dr Bird. Papa.

subject: Zella Douglas
statement: Envelope postmarked Union City, CA., 7 Sept 1923, to Zella Douglas, Red Oak
verbatim_quotation: Zella Douglas / Red Oak — / Texas — / UNION CITY / SEP 7 / 12:30 AM / CA. / 1923

subject: Mrs Henderson; Ernest; Bruce; Ira; Van
statement: Household at Union City; Ernest's cotton; Bruce may want the car; Ira's condition
verbatim_quotation: I gave Mrs Henderson the suit case. ... If Ernest wants to kill one and peddle it out ... If Bruce wants the car very much, he will get rid of his and buy ... Very sorry to hear of Ira's condition. ... Have Ernest and Van to make a careful estimate of the cotton crop in Bales.

subject: Union City prices
statement: Apples $1-1.50/bushel, cider 50c-$1/gallon, pears $1-1.50/bushel
verbatim_quotation: Good apples here sell from a dollar to a dollar and a half per bushel. Cider fifty cents to a dollar per gallon. Pears 1.00 to 1.50 per bushel.

subject: Papa
statement: Last plug removed; hole in cheek made by the cancer coming out; lump under chin like a small butter bean
verbatim_quotation: The last plug is removed, and future treatments not needed unless more Metastasis sets up. ... It will take a long time to heal the hole in my cheek made by the cancer coming out ... The lump under my chin is gradually getting less, thinner and flatter, about like a small butter bean.

subject: Mr. Ridley; Mrs. Johnson
statement: Fellow patients
verbatim_quotation: Mr. Ridley is improving right along ... Mrs. Johnson is getting along very slowly.

subject: Papa
statement: House repairs: ceil, paper or paint; about fifty dollars; Ernest to bring lumber for scaffolding
verbatim_quotation: There is three ways to stop this. Ceil over the old ceiling with new lumber, paper or paint the walls. ... Oil, paint, and putting it on, will likely cost about fifty dollars

subject: Papa
statement: Labor scarce; racial remark retained as documentary text
verbatim_quotation: White folks wont work [[inserted: or dont work]], and niggers are scarce. I do not know when I have seen a white man hunting work.

subject: Zella Douglas
statement: Envelope Union City GA [sic] AUG 30 1923
verbatim_quotation: UNION CITY / AUG 30 / 6 PM / GA / 1923

subject: Papa
statement: Aug 30 1923: most of the cancer came out; home maybe middle of October
verbatim_quotation: Most of the cancer came out, a little left, cant tell just how much. ... If no further trouble comes up, and I stay until fully healed, it may be the middle of October

subject: Papa; Mr. Ligon; Guaranty Trust bank of Waxahachie
statement: Note due 11 Sept at Guaranty Trust bank; tax receipt to Farrar and Kemble attorneys for the suit in the [[Funds?]] tax business; Buord Farrar attorney
verbatim_quotation: go to Mr. Ligon, get the note on The Guaranty Trust bank of Waxahachie, due the eleventh day of September ... take it Farrar and Kemble attys, and leave with them. They may want / it as evidence in the suit pending in the [[Funds?]] tax business. / Then tell Buord Farrar to check on Red Oak for what funds he may have to have in my case as attorney.

subject: Stoker
statement: Made an awful charge overhauling the machine
verbatim_quotation: Stoker made an awful charge. Did he itemize it? He must have overhauled the whole machine.

subject: Allie
statement: Going to Gunter to take charge of a dormitory; she has cancer
verbatim_quotation: Allie is making ready to go to Gunter, take charge of a Dormitory, and put the children in school. ... She has cancer

subject: Duckworth; the A.W.
statement: Duckworth made business manager of the A.W.; circular calling for help to print it
verbatim_quotation: Duckworth has been made business manager of the A.W. He has put out a circular letter to the brethren, calling for help to print it in Texas saying he has no money and that the paper has none

subject: Henry Douglas; N. L. Douglas
statement: Identifying slip: letter to Mr. N. L. Douglas from son Henry, Palestine; a second slip: letters by Henry and Ellen Douglas
verbatim_quotation: To Mr. N. L. Douglas / from son, / Henry Douglas / Palestine, Texas / Sept. 8, 1851 / Letters written by / Henry and Ellen Douglas

subject: Henry Douglas; sister Rebecca
statement: Henry writing to 'sister Rebecca'
verbatim_quotation: I have just been writing to sister Rebecca, and scolded a good deal with [[her?]] for none of you writing to me

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: Palestine (Anderson County) sickly for two months, more than he ever saw in Ellis Co.; Old Mr Benson
verbatim_quotation: This County although reputed to be one of the healthiest in the State, has been very sickly for two months past, more so than I ever saw it in Ellis Co. I think that Old Mr Benson is nearly willing to try the [[illegible]] again

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: Quit Mr Dale; helping [[Hedlie?]] a large livery stable; wages $1.50 per day, board $10 per month; carpenters' opening; journeywork or undertaker
verbatim_quotation: I quit working for Mr Dale about a month ago ... I am now helping [[Hedlie?]] a large Livery Stable, my wages are $1,50 cts pr day, but after subtracting $10 pr month for board & washing, the amount is considerably diminished. There is going to be a very good opening for carpenters here this coming Winter and Spring, and I am somewhat at a loss whether to continue journeywork or turn out undertaker

subject: Christian Church at Palestine
statement: Resolved to build a house of worship 56 by 34 feet
verbatim_quotation: The Christian Church at this place have resolved to build a house of worship as soon as lumber can be procured. It will be 56 ft long & 34 wide

subject: Mr Mallard
statement: Bound for old Rutherford; wife wants Tennessee
verbatim_quotation: I was at Mr Mallards house a time ago, he says he is bound for old Rutherford as soon as he can get off ... his wife is very much dissatisfied and cant hear to nothing else but going back to Tenn.

subject: Susannah
statement: Henry rejoices at Susannah's [obedience to] the Truth
verbatim_quotation: Nothing gratified me more than to hear of Susannahs [[illegible]] the Truth, may she hold out faithful to the end is my sincere prayer. O that all the Family that have arrived at the years of discretion were gathered into the fold of Christ.

subject: Ellen Douglas; Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slip: to Sister Lizzie Douglas from Ellen Douglas
verbatim_quotation: To Sister Lizzie Douglas / from / Ellen Douglas / Jan. 12, 1862

subject: Ellen Douglas
statement: Christmas 1861 at her cabin: cake, pies, egg nog, 14 young people; young men left for the war
verbatim_quotation: I had plenty of cake and pies at my cabin Christmas day and a big Egg nog. ... I looked out and saw 14 young men and girls riged out comeing ... all the week after which most all the young men left for the war.

subject: [[Gaskin?]]; Angus; Maggie; Sister Fleming; heath
statement: Ellen's children and household
verbatim_quotation: [[Gaskin?]] had a chill last week and now has very sore eyes he is walking and is as pretty as any bodys boy he can talk now as good as Angus. Maggie is growing fast and will be another Sister Fleming ... my man Angus is as fat as a pig

subject: Warren; Beck
statement: Warren gone to Deer Creek to move Beck there; going to the war as soon as she is confined; baby expected 5-11 Feb 1862
verbatim_quotation: Beck has not been very well ... Warren had gone to deer creek to see about moveing her there as he is going to the war as soon as she is confined they will not break up housekeeping until after that, she is expecting about the 5 to the 11 of Feb.

subject: Beck (Rebecca); Warren
statement: Warren tried to get some of her sisters to stay with her; Ellen offers
verbatim_quotation: Warren tryed to get some of her sisters to come home with him and stay a while with her but they could not leave home

subject: Ellen Douglas
statement: Living in Sam's cabin; Sue's house commenced
verbatim_quotation: we are still in Sams cabin I expect I will remain here some time yet ... Tell Sue I am glad to hear of her hopes being realized that is her house comenced

subject: Amanda Berry; Lizzie West
statement: Neighbours who want letters from Laura
verbatim_quotation: tell Laura the last time I saw Amanda Berry she asked about her and said she must write to her Lizzie West was here not long ago

subject: Warren; Beck
statement: Warren will leave as soon as Beck is able to be moved to her father's
verbatim_quotation: I recon you will all come now to see Warren before he goes off he will leave as soon as beck is able for him to move her to her fathers.

subject: H. Douglas
statement: Went to Brushy to secure 'the Land' but failed to get the certificate; dated Buchanan
verbatim_quotation: I started yesterday to Brushy to see if I could secure the Land [[illegible]] you, but failed to get the certificate him as I expected ... Buchanan Jany 15th 1862 H. Douglas

subject: Warren
statement: Warren likely to get off in February; company not yet chosen
verbatim_quotation: Warren is likely to get off in Feb — does not know what Co he will join yet

subject: H. Douglas
statement: Wool sent to Shreveport netted 26 cents
verbatim_quotation: I sent [[752?]] lbs wool to Shriveport it netted 26 cts

subject: Henry Douglas; Lizzie
statement: Slip: to Sister Lizzie (possibly while in California) from Henry Douglas, Red Oak
verbatim_quotation: To Sister Lizzie / (possibly while in California) / from Henry Douglas / Red Oak, Texas / Sept. 6, 1892

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: On irreligion in California; 'California & Sodom & Gomorrah are not unlike'
verbatim_quotation: I do not now wish to say anything only to regret, nay lament such a condition of irreligion as portrayed in your letter Surely California & Sodom & Gomorrah are not unlike / A day in the courts of the Lord is surely worth a thousand in such a place

subject: Liberty; Bros Cole & Graves
statement: Good meeting at Liberty; Clarence & Kate obeyed the gospel; they will be 14 on 8 Sept [1892]
verbatim_quotation: We have just had a good meeting at Liberty conducted by Bros Cole & Graves / You will rejoice with me that Clarence & Kate obeyed the gospel. They will be 14 the 8th inst

subject: Otis Maynard?; Lee Weatherford?; Robbie Sullivan?; Jesse Graves; Mrs Bur Pratts?
statement: Others added at the meeting; 'your son'
verbatim_quotation: Also your son, [[Or. Otis Maynard?]] Lee [[Weatherford?]] Robbie [[Sullivan?]] Jesse Graves & Mrs [[Bur Pratts?]] & others unknown to you

subject: Crops 1892
statement: Corn good, wheat and oats fine, cotton average; Mr Ward a good renter for Lizzie
verbatim_quotation: Our Wheat & Oats were fine & Cotton a good average Many are picking & the gin whistles are beginning to sound ... Mr Ward has a good crop for you I think he is a good renter

subject: Henry Allen; Sam Strand?; Mrs Bell; Mrs Thuston?; Dr Duff; Henry Orr
statement: Tenancy changes
verbatim_quotation: Henry Allen is going to move to Hood County near Acton & Sam [[Strand?]] has rented Mrs Bells place Mrs [[Thuston?]] has rented Dr Duffs & her son in law [[Surren?]] Henry Orrs place

subject: Jodie
statement: In bad health; went to Erath Co.; Greer Co. crops failed
verbatim_quotation: Jodie is in bad health as usual & started yesterday to Erath Co. Greer Co failed on crops this year

subject: Billy Davis
statement: Fell off his wagon near Palmer
verbatim_quotation: Billy Davis fell off his wagon [[illegible]] [[near?]] [[Palmer?]] about 10 days ago.

subject: Tom & Laura; John & Ann; Sue; Kate; Mr & Mrs Barton
statement: Family in California and Brushy
verbatim_quotation: Give my love to Tom & Laura & family & also to John & Ann ... Sue will probably teach in Brushy this winter & I will send Kate to her / Give to Mr & Mrs Barton / Your brother Henry

subject: Henry Douglas; Mary Douglas
statement: Slip: to Mrs Mary (N. L.) Douglas from Henry, Palestine, Dec. 30 1853 (letter reads Dec. 3d)
verbatim_quotation: To Mrs Mary (N. L.) / Douglas / From Henry Douglas. / Palestine, Tex / Dec. 30, 1853 ... Palestine Dec. 3d 1853 / Dear Mother

subject: Jepse; Warren
statement: Gone out on the Brazos; Warren's second trip
verbatim_quotation: I learned from him some of the particulars about home, & amongst the rest, that Jepse & Warren had gone out on / Brazos. ... Warren has been writing a little about his trip to the Brazos, but only casually alluded to his second trip

subject: David Gaslin
statement: Met at Bonners ferry on Trinity
verbatim_quotation: I had however the pleasure of meeting with David Gaslin, at Bonners ferry on Trinity, last monday evening

subject: Palestine cooperation meeting
statement: About $450 subscribed for evangelizing; committee of 5 managers; Bro. Kendrick preached; [[6?]] baptized incl. Addison son of Bro Clark and Albert son of Bro. K
verbatim_quotation: The Co-operation will, I think be quite effective; about 450 dols were subscribed for evangelizing purposes ... Bro. Kendrick had all the preaching to do. There were [[6?]] baptized & one other added to the Church 2 of them were little boys, one, Addison, son of Bro Clark aged about 12 years the other Albert, Bro. K's oldest son about 10 years old.

subject: Mrs Mary Douglas
statement: Address Red Oak Texas
verbatim_quotation: Mrs Mary Douglas / Red Oak Texas

subject: Henry Douglas; N. L. Douglas
statement: Slip: to N. L. Douglas from Henry Douglas, Palestine
verbatim_quotation: To N. L. Douglas / from Henry Douglas / Palestine, Tex. / Jan. 12, 1855

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: Left home in October [1854]; decided to remain in Palestine one more year; partnership with Dr Kendrick, one-third of accounts and expense
verbatim_quotation: I concluded to remain here one year longer, & risk the consequences. Dr Kendrick & myself have formed a partnership for the year. I get ⅓ of the accounts, & am at ⅓ the expence, pay my board & furnish my own horse

subject: Old Mr Ransom
statement: Known to N. L. Douglas; will try Dr K.
verbatim_quotation: Old Mr Ransom, (whom I take to be a man of strong prejudices) has declared his intention to try Dr K when next he wants a physician. ... I mention him, as he is known to you

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: Wrote to Warren of a cancer case; promises a visit in April
verbatim_quotation: I wrote to Warren, of a Cancer case we have on hand ... I think I can venture to promise you a visit in the Spring, say April.

subject: Henry Douglas; Mary Douglas; Susannah
statement: Letter from Mary and Susannah; Uncle Sam's court engagements; Jepie's and Warren's absences; Susannah to come down with Henry
verbatim_quotation: The letter from yourself & Susannah, came by last mail ... I recd a letter from Uncle Sam a short time ago, suggesting the 1st of May ... in consequence of his engagements, at court in April & also Jepie's & Warrens absences ... I am pleased that Susannah has consented to come down with me

subject: Henry Douglas; N. L. Douglas
statement: Parting from Father near the Willow pond; walked to Porters Bluff
verbatim_quotation: I know that while memory lasts I shall never forget the day when I parted from Father, in the wide lonely prairie, near the Willow pond, his parting advice, & the loneliness of the subsequent hours in walking to Porters Bluff. Never till then had I felt so isolated; never had I felt what it was to be homeless, houseless, & in effect, friendless

subject: Weather 1853
statement: Dry; corn frostbitten; wheat feared ruined
verbatim_quotation: The weather has been very dry with us, for a long time, & crops are suffering greatly for rain. Corn has been badly frostbitten ... I fear the wheat has been ruined, with you.

subject: aunt Cynthia
statement: Postscript: remember me to [[Un.?]] & aunt Cynthia
verbatim_quotation: P.S. Give my love to all. Remember me to [[Un.?]] & aunt Cynthia. &c &c / H.D.

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: Slip: driving a herd of sheep to Texas from Mississippi County, Missouri
verbatim_quotation: To N. L. Douglas / from / Henry Douglas / Mississippi County, / Missouri / June 23, 1860 / — re driving herd of / sheep to Texas

subject: Henry Douglas; Willis Helm
statement: Paid $1-2 per sheep; Willis Helm sent $500; with $1500 bought 750 head; about $200 left
verbatim_quotation: I have had to pay from 1 to 2 dollars for sheep ... Mr Willis Helm sent $500 by me to get him some sheep & with the 1500 I have bought 750 head & do not know that I will have money enough to get them to Tex. as I only have some 200 left.

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: Bought sheep in Callaway & Graves Co's Ky and Christian Co; crossed the Mississippi at the Iron Banks; ferriage 8 cts per head
verbatim_quotation: I bought common sheep in Callaway & Graves Co's Ky purchase lambs at 1 & Ewes at 1.25 per head ... went back to Christian Co & got some 250 head at 1.75 & 2 per head ... I crossed the Mississippi at the Iron Banks last Sunday & had to pay 8 cts per head ferriage

subject: Sheep drove
statement: Lost near 50 head; disease; a drove from Rutherford Co Tennessee passed
verbatim_quotation: Several have died & altogether I have lost near 50 head since I started ... A few days ago a drove of 7 or 800 passed from Rutherford Co Tennessee & lost a great many.

subject: Henry Douglas
statement: 4 hands hired at $15 per month; route via Fort Gibson ferry on the Arkansas and Springfield Mo.
verbatim_quotation: I have 4 hands hired at 15 dollars per month each & taking all together I cannot make the drove profitable if I do not lose by it. I have not heard from any of you since I left Texas nor have I heard from Ellen since I left Lincoln County. ... I suppose I will reach Springfield Mo. in 30 or 40 days

subject: Ellen
statement: Henry has not heard from Ellen since leaving Lincoln County
verbatim_quotation: nor have I heard from Ellen since I left Lincoln County

subject: Samuel Wallace; N. L. Douglas
statement: Promissory note: five barrels corn or four dollars by 25 Dec next
verbatim_quotation: By the 25th December next I promise to pay to N L Douglas at his house five barrels corn, or four Dollars, value recd this 2nd Oct. 1832. / Samuel Wallace [[seal]]

subject: James Bass; N. L. Douglas
statement: Business letter from Murfreesboro; two to three years since he heard from Douglas about 'our business'
verbatim_quotation: It has been about two years since I heard from you in relation to our business — it has been I believe nearly three years.

subject: James Bass; Gen. A. Sublett
statement: Bass bought the balance of the Littleton White tract, about 3250 acres; wants Douglas to see whether taxes are paid; Louis Dickson tract on the Trinity at the mouth of five mile creek
verbatim_quotation: I have bought lately of Gen. A. Sublett the balance of the Littleton White tract of Land — the purchase embraces about thirty two hundred & fifty acres — You know where it is situated & I want you to see to it. See whether the Taxes are paid ... the Louis Dickson tract of Land on the Trinity River ... I believe the Land is at the mouth of the five mile [[deleted: branch?]] [[inserted: creek]]

subject: Nathaniel Douglas
statement: Addressed 'Nathaniel Douglas, Red Oak Post Office, Texas'
verbatim_quotation: Nathaniel Douglas / Red Oak Post Office / Texas.

subject: [[S. A.?]] Farrar; F. L. Farrar; G. A. Sublett
statement: Note for $520 to Sublett due 1 March next; $15 received by N. L. Douglas for Sublett; endorsed to Mr [[Ledbetter?]]
verbatim_quotation: On or before the first day of March next I promise G. A. Sublett to pay him or order Five Hundred and twenty Dollars value received ... This the 12th day of October 1852 / [[S. A.?]] Farrar / F. L. Farrar ... April 20th 1853 / Received on the within Note Fifteen dollars. N L Douglas / for G. A. Sublett ... Pay the within to Mr [[Ledbetter?]] ... 1852 oct 28th / Geo A Sublett

subject: N L Douglas as agent for G A Sublett; W. B. McCabe
statement: Redemption of 1280 acres on Subletts Creek listed to A J Porter, sold for 1848 taxes on 4 Feb 1850 to C M Winkler; tax and cost $14.48; Winkler releases claim 31 Jan 1851
verbatim_quotation: Rit of Revocation / of / A J Porter 1280 acres / Land Taxes & cost / paid up to 1850 / Tax and cost $14.48 ... N L Douglas as agent for G A Sublett has this day paid me the amount of Tax and Cost of Sale and one hundred per cent there and as required by Law for the Redemption of 1280 acres of Land lying on Subletts Creek and sold by me for the Taxes for the year 1848 [[inserted: and listed to A J Porter]] on the fourth day of February AD 1850 and purchased by C M Winkler ... W. B. McCabe [[seal]] / assessor & collector / for the county Navarro ... I ratify and sanction the doings of W. B. McCabe ... Jany 31st 1851 / C M Winkler

subject: [[S W?]] Webber; N. L. Douglas
statement: Due bill for five dollars
verbatim_quotation: Due N. L. Douglas or bearer five dollars value received. January. 21st 1829. / [[S W?]] Webber

subject: Geo A Sublett; N L Douglas
statement: Power of attorney from Sublett of Rutherford County, Tennessee to 'my friend N L Douglas of Ellis County' to sell lands in Dallas, Ellis and Navarro counties; conveyance to Mr. Farro of 640 acres; to Ephraim Andrews & Co. 540 acres in two surveys
verbatim_quotation: I Geo A Sublett of the County of Rutherford and State of Tennessee have nominated and appointed, made and constituted my friend N L Douglas of Ellis County State of Texas, my true and lawful attorney for me, and in my name to bargain Sell Grant and convey ... any part or all of the lands that, I own in the State of Texas — in the Counties of Dallas, Ellis, and Navaro ... likewise to make proper conveyance to Mr. Farro for a tract of Six hundred and forty acres heretofore Sold him, also to Ephraim Andrews & Co. Five hundred and Forty acres in two Seperate Surveys.

subject: Benj F Hawkins
statement: Clerk of the County Court of Ellis County; power of attorney recorded 8 Nov 1852 in Deed Record A page 163
date_as_written: 29th day of October AD 1852; November 8th A.D. 1852
verbatim_quotation: Benj F Hawkins Clerk of the County Court of Ellis County ... the within power of attorney was duly duly Recorded November 8th A.D. 1852 at 9 O.clock A.M. in Deed Record A page 163.

subject: G. Douglas
statement: Typed poem 'There is a lonliness of heart' dated 1867
verbatim_quotation: There is a lonliness of heart / No words can ere express, / Too deep for sorrow's tears to start / To relieve the aching breast. ... 1867 G. Douglas

subject: Robert Crow; G A Sublett
statement: Crow of Leon County sells 1280 acres (Jasper County certificate 2d Class No 246 of 10 Jan 1840) to Sublett for $160; acknowledged before David M. Brown, Chief Justice, 22 May 1849; recorded Navarro Co. Book A pp. 433-34 on 14 Dec 1849
verbatim_quotation: I Robert Crow for and in consideration of the sum of one hundred and Sixty dollars to me in hand paid by G A Sublett ... all that tract lot or parcel of land containing twelve hundred and Eighty acres being the same secured to me the said Crow by virtue of a certificate issued by the board of land commissioners for Jasper County on the tenth day of January AD 1840 — 2d Class No 246 ... Before me David M. Brown Chief Justice and Exofficio Notary public ... Recorded the 14th day of December A.D. 1849 in Book A, pages 433 & 34 / R [[H?]] White Clk Navarro Co

subject: N L Douglas as agent for G A Sublett
statement: Redemption of 640 acres granted to Robert Crow, sold 25 July 1850 for 1849 taxes; total $3.08; W B McCabe, 3 Feb 1851; recorded Navarro Book C p. 181
verbatim_quotation: N L Douglas as agent for G A Sublett has this day paid to me the undersigned assessor & Collector ... for the Redemption of 640 acres of Land granted to Robert Crow and Given in by G A Sublett for Taxes for the year 1849 and Sold by me for the Taxes for the year 1849 on the 25th day of July AD 1850 and bid off to the State ... Total amount of all | $3.08 ... this 3d day of February AD 1851 / W B McCabe

subject: Sarah Gail (Douglas) Headrick; Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slip: to Miss Lizzie Douglas from niece Sarah Gail (Douglas) Headrick, Bardsdale, Calif; envelope 'from Sadie' to Miss Lizzie Douglas, Ferris, Ellis Co.
verbatim_quotation: To Miss Lizzie Douglas / from Niece / Sarah Gail (Douglas) Headrick / Bardsdale, Calif / [[Sat?]] 29, 1893 ... from Sadie / Miss Lizzie Douglas / Ferris / Ellis Co. / Texas / BARDSDALE AUG 9 [[1894?]] CAL.

subject: Sadie Headrick
statement: Letter from Bardsdale; 'haven't had a break down since I wrote last'; sitting-room furnishings; the store
verbatim_quotation: Bardsdale, Sep, 29th, 1893. / My Dear Aunt:—I finished up my morning work pretty well this forenoon ... I am still better—haven't had a "break down" since I wrote last.

subject: Bruce; Elmo; Mr. Headrick
statement: Sadie's children Bruce and Elmo; Mr. Headrick down with his back; Grandma [[Chadens?]]'s house; Mrs. [[Scholl?]] to Kansas
verbatim_quotation: One day he came from the P.O. & said "Grandma [[Chadens?]] house isn't togezzer is it Mamma?" ... Mr. Headrick has been down with his back, for two weeks ... Mrs. [[Scholl?]] started back to Kansas the 19th.

subject: Sadie Headrick
statement: Dreamed of the old homestead, telling 'you & Grandma my troubles', and of Uncle [[George?]]
verbatim_quotation: I dreamed, last night of being at the old homestead, & telling you & Grandma my troubles, as I was wont to do in by-gone days & also of seeing Uncle [[George?]] ... A few nights before I dreamed of Grandma.

subject: Elmo
statement: Elmo's joke about Mr. [[McKie's?]] cow
verbatim_quotation: along came Mr. [[McKie's?]] cow—Elmo remarked if that cow was married, she would have a calf. (with her he meant) Making that a [[test?]] most of the California cows are unmarried.

subject: Advocate; D. L.; Uncle Geo.; Bro. Polly
statement: Article in the Advocate of April 13 by D. L.; Uncle Geo.'s announcement of the [[Elmwood?]] camp-meeting; Bro. Polly's meetings
verbatim_quotation: There is a thought contained in the piece headed "A [[Lyffe?]]" (in Advocate of April 13th) by D. L. ... Saw in my last paper, the announcement, by Uncle Geo. of the [[Elmwood?]] camp-meeting—How I wish I could attend as of old. Remember me to Bro. Polly

subject: Kate [[Larson?]]; Mr. H.
statement: Kate stayed while Mr. H. went to Los Angeles; 20 dozen eggs to count
verbatim_quotation: Last week Mr. H. went to Los Angeles—Kate [[Larson?]] staid with me, Bruce was sick with cold & fever ... in came over 20 doz. eggs to be counted

subject: Sadie Headrick
statement: Refuses life insurance on religious convictions
verbatim_quotation: a Life Insurance Agent & tried to get me to influence Mr. H. to insure. I told him 'twas against my religious convictions He said "christianity would never keep you from starving to death besides the majority of christians favored it" I told him the "majority" were on their way to perdition too.

subject: Mrs. Timmons; Ellen
statement: Mrs. Timmons abed with nervous prostration; 'Now you & Ellen shake your sides'
verbatim_quotation: Now you & Ellen shake your sides. / Last monday week, I went up to Mrs. Timmons & found her abed with nervous prostration

subject: (Sarah) Sadie Gail Douglas Headrick; Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slip: to Miss Lizzie Douglas (aunt) from Sadie, Bardsdale, Aug. 8
verbatim_quotation: To Miss Lizzie Douglas / (aunt) / from / (Sarah) Sadie Gail / Douglas Headrick / Bardsdale / Aug. 8

subject: Grandma Humphrey; Dr. [[Hinckley?]]; Drs. Bard and Mott
statement: Grandma Humphrey's growth; operation
verbatim_quotation: Grandma Humphrey's growth increases, and is so bad she has difficulty in breathing—consequently has consented to have an operation performed ... Dr. [[Hinckley?]] is back now and he Drs. Bard and Mott, are to do the work.

subject: Picnic at Mr. Grimes'
statement: Mr. Wigmore's cart; Mrs. Pickering; Mr. Henry Chadsey in Mrs. [[Curren's?]] surrey; Lillie Chadsey
verbatim_quotation: We had our picnic at Mr. Grimes, last saturday ... if I didn't go down and ask Mr. Wigmore for his cart ... I found Mrs. Pickering hardly able to be out of bed ... down came Mr. Henry Chadsey in Mrs. [[Curren's?]] surrey, for us. Lillie Chadsey had inquired of several why I wasn't there ... They had lemonade and ice-cream. two swings a set of croquet, and a game of baseball.

subject: little [[Beckie's?]]
statement: Married at Santa Paula on her 18th birthday to Mr. [[Reck?]] [[Lehock?]] unbeknown to her father; Grandma Roberts
verbatim_quotation: That was the 4th, and little [[Beckie's?]] birthday, and what think you, she went to Santa Paula with Mr. [[Reck?]] [[Lehock?]] and married him unbeknowing to her father. ... It was her 18th birthday. ... Grandma Roberts spent last sunday night with us.

subject: Sadie Headrick
statement: Earned $4.50 pitting fruit
verbatim_quotation: Well I must tell you that I earned $4.50 pitting fruit. A handsome amount for me.

subject: Mrs. Sara Headrick
statement: Envelope to Mrs. Sara Headrick, Red Oak, Texas; postage due 2 cents; postmark [[SANTA BARBARA CAL.?]] APR 27 1921
verbatim_quotation: Mrs. Sara Headrick / Red Oak. / Texas. / POSTAGE DUE 2 CENTS / [[SANTA BARBARA CAL.?]] APR 27 6:30 PM 1921

subject: Mrs. Weatherford; Cousin Sarah Jeter
statement: Warning about 'that son of hers'
verbatim_quotation: I think I have heard Mrs. Weatherford speak of Cousin Sarah Jeter, and I must caution you right here, not to allow your-self to become too much infatuated with that son of hers

subject: Mr. [[Annis?]]; Clapp ranch; church organ
statement: Clapp ranch bought for $1500; $35 subscribed and $50 from Mr. Bard for a new church organ
verbatim_quotation: Mr. [[Annis?]] has bought the Clapp ranch over the mountains. Payed $1500. When Mr. [[Clapp?]] left, he sold the church organ—So Kate Burdick Wheeler & Mary Yeager, set to work to raise money to buy another. They succeeded in getting $35 subscribed & Mr. Bard, who owns so much land here, sent a check for $50

subject: Mr. Pickering; Holiness sermon
statement: Bible study proposal; Holiness sermon on sanctification and quitting tobacco
verbatim_quotation: Mr. Pickering, our Supt and the only one in the School, who knows anything about the Bible, suggested, that we older ones get together once a week, and study by subjects ... Last sunday we had a Holiness sermon ... the crowning point of his being sanctified was quitting tobacco.

subject: Mrs. [[Wigart?]]
statement: Does not think water baptism essential; expects the spirit as a dove
verbatim_quotation: she doesn't think water baptism, at all, essential to salvation; but still she thinks perhaps, sometime, she will be immersed—adding, she always had an idea if she ever did, the spirit would descend on her, in the shape of a dove

subject: Fannie
statement: Slip: part of a letter from Fannie mentioning Lizzie & Laura; page 4 mentions Johnson Co. and [[Evan?]]
verbatim_quotation: Part of letter – / Mentions / Lizzie & Laura / from Fannie ... one of the prettiest looking [[little?]] [[fellows?]] that left Johnson Co. ... I must to write a letter to [[Evan?]] to night.

subject: Mollie (Woodbury, Tenn.)

verbatim_quotation: Miss Lizzie Douglas. / Redoak / Texas / WOODBURY APR 10 TEN. ... Poem to / Miss Lizzie Douglas / From Mollie / Woodbury, Tenn.

subject: Mollie; Cousin George
statement: Manuscript of 'Just before the battle Mother' written by request for Cousin George
verbatim_quotation: Just before the battle Mother / I am thinking most of you ... Written by request Dec 9th /66 For Cousin George / Mollie

subject: George Douglas
statement: Slip: 'Concerning Uncle George Douglas – his work at Sylvanna Church – his death Sept. 23, 1923'
verbatim_quotation: Concerning Uncle / George Douglas / – his work at / Sylvanna Church / – his death / Sept. 23, 1923

subject: George Douglas
statement: Continued his labors with the Church at Sylvana until his death 23 Sept 1923; opposed the Sunday School but did not withdraw; died in Georgia
verbatim_quotation: My father continued his labors with the Church at Sylvana until his death Sept 23 1923. Though opposing the Sunday School he did not withdraw from the congregation but endeavored to present the truth as he understood it. His health became impaired and he realized that his work was done. He died in Ga and

subject: George Douglas; Sylvana congregation
statement: Brought back and buried from the Church; strong character; after his death the congregation ceased to meet
verbatim_quotation: was brought back and buried from the Church that had been his life work. / He was a strong character and was [[inserted: in full sense an excellent leader]] While in his prime to direct the affairs of the Church, he was unable to train anyone to take his place and after his death the congregation was torn by dissensions and after a few years ceased to consistently meet

subject: Poem
statement: 'In Answer to the Author of "Georgie"' (manuscript verse)
verbatim_quotation: In answer to the Author of "Georgie." / I seek not for devoted dears.— / "Platonic friendship at my years," / Most surely will suffice

subject: Song ballad
statement: 'Swinging in the lane', docketed Jan the 22, 1881; Rosa Nell; Aunt Jemima Brown
verbatim_quotation: Song Ballad / Jan the 22, / 1881. / Swinging in the lane. ... Was introduced to Rosa Nell / By Aunt Jemima Brown

subject: Sarah E. Douglas
statement: Essay 'The beauty of female culture' signed Sarah E. Douglas, April [[21?]]
verbatim_quotation: The Beauty of Culture / by Sarah Douglas ... There is nothing more important than the cultivation of our minds ... Sarah E. Douglas / April [[21?]].

subject: Emma Bell
statement: Composition 'Parting from Friends' marked 'Very good'
verbatim_quotation: Composition / "Parting from Friends" / by Emma Bell ... O! how sad we feel when we part from our dear friends! ... Very good

verbatim_quotation: To Mrs. (Mary) Douglas & / Cynthia Orr – daughters / of Rebecca Goodloe / from / B. F. Wright) / Jacob Wright, brother of Rebecca Wright Goodloe.] / – Decree appealed by Mr. Lillard – / – Shows Jacob Wright & Wife were cousins – / Rebecca Alexander their daughter, being equal heir of the father & mother of Mary Wright.

subject: Mrs. Douglas; Mrs. Orr
statement: Addressed at Ferris, Texas; envelope postmarked Ferris Dec 8 1883
verbatim_quotation: FERRIS, / DEC / 8 / 1883 / TEX. ... Mrs. Douglas and Mrs. Orr. / Ferris, Texas.

subject: Chancellor Burton
statement: Sick and died during the term; a Circuit Court judge decided the case
verbatim_quotation: During the Term of the Court, Chancellor Burton was sick and died. While he was sick a Circuit Court Judge held his Court and decided the case as to who the land goes to, but seemed very much tangled in the case.

subject: Rebecca Alexander estate
statement: 180 acres from her father Jacob Wright to his ~40 nephews and nieces (17 living, 23 dead); the McGlothlin tract of 230/235 acres from her mother 'ascends' to heirs of Mary Wright; parents were cousins
verbatim_quotation: He decided that 180 Acres of the land that descended to Mrs. Alexander from her father, Jacob Wright, goes to or is inherited by the nephews and nieces of Jacob Wright ... as he had about forty nephews and nieces, seventeen of whom are living, and about twenty three dead ... As to the McGlothlin tract of 230 Acres, descended to Mrs. Alexander from her mother ... the father and mother being cousins

subject: B. F. Lillard
statement: Appealed to the Supreme Court; 'Per Ida'
verbatim_quotation: I appealed from the whole decree to the Supreme Court as also did the McGlothlin claimants ... Very Respectfully, / B. F. Lillard. / Per Ida.

subject: Mary Douglas; B. F. Lillard
statement: Draft power of attorney: Mary Douglas of Ellis County appoints Lillard to demand her distributive share in the real estate descended to her from Mrs Rebecca T. Alexander, late of Rutherford County, Tennessee
verbatim_quotation: I Mrs Mary Douglas of said County and State do hereby nominate and appoint B. F. Lillard of Murfreesboro Tenn, my true and lawful Attorney ... the distributive share or interest in the real estate that descended to me from Mrs Rebecca T. Alexander, late of Rutherford County and State of Tennessee, now deceased

subject: M. M. Dill; George Douglas; Cynthia Orr; Docia Bivins; Isaac N. Wright; Mrs. Nance; Mandy
statement: Dill ('Your Cousin') writes to George at Ferris; heirs named
verbatim_quotation: Mr Lillard our Attorney has shown me a letter from you in answer to two letters that I requested him to write to your Mother and Cousin Cynthia Orr ... I have conferred with Cousin Docia Bivins, she stated that she was going to leave her part, I have also conferred with Isaac N. Wright ... he has recd a letter from Mrs Nance ... Isaac Wright recd a letter from his sister Mandy ... Your Cousin / M M Dill.

subject: Rebecca Alexander estate
statement: 640 acre tract sold by Alexander & wife; the River Tract & the Arkansas lands
verbatim_quotation: We will not at present take any steps against the 640 Acre Tract of land sold by Alexander & wife ... The River Tract & the Arkansas lands will no doubt be surrendered up

subject: Mary Douglas; Rebecca Alexander; Jacob Wright
statement: Lillard: Mrs Alexander was 'your Cousin ... daughter of your uncle Jacob Wright'; heirs are first cousins: 3 Goodloe, 3 Dill, 2 Brasher, 6 Thompson Wright
verbatim_quotation: I suppose that you have heard of the death of your Cousin Mrs Alexander daughter of your uncle Jacob Wright. She did not make a will and her real estate descends to her next of kin consisting of her first Cousins now living being 3 of the Goodloe family, three of the Dill, two of the Brasher and six of the Thompson Wright family

subject: Rebecca Alexander estate
statement: 680 acres assessed at $8500; probably 300 acres in Arkansas; 640 acres sold for $6400 on 1-3 years' credit; conveyance defective
verbatim_quotation: the real estate consisting of 680 Acres of land assessed at $8500.00 but of course land generally brings double the assessment ... probably 300 Acres in Ark. ... The 640 Acres sold as above referred to was sold in order to convert the property as I have been informed for $6400.00 rather a depreciated price on one two and three years credit ... The conveyance is defective

subject: Mary Douglas
statement: Post office corrected from Ennis to Ferris; letter returned after 28 days
verbatim_quotation: [[deleted: Ennis]] [[inserted: Ferris]] Texas ... The above letter was mailed and directed to Ennis and after 28 days returned to me. I now learn that your Post Office is Ferris

subject: B. F. Lillard; George Douglas
statement: George's letter of 15 March 1883 questioned Lillard; Lillard's defence; twenty-five years at the bar; Judge Peter Turney of Winchester; Judge Burton; John Woods; Col. N. D. Robinson; whisky prescribed for neuralgic rheumatism from army wounds
verbatim_quotation: Your letter of March 15th has been recd. I think that you have been under a misapprehension about several things ... I have referred you to Judge Peter Turney of Winchester Tenn ... my Law Diploma was signed 25 years ago by Judges Green & Caruthers of Cumberland University ... whisky for neuralgic rheumatism ... caused from Army wounds

subject: Albert Jetton
statement: 'your Cousin Albert Jetton whose store is within 75-ft of that Law Office'; recommends Lillard as 'Your Nephew'
verbatim_quotation: Why did not Mr. Alexander bring into the Consultation your Cousin Albert Jetton whose store is within 75-ft of that Law Office ... I take pleasure in recommending him to you / Your Nephew Albert Jetton ... I do not advise a Suit but only recommend Mr Lillard as a Lawyer / Yours A Jetton

subject: D Travis; A. M. Alexander; D. M. McKnight
statement: 640 acre tract conveyed to D Travis for $6400 in three payments Aug 1882-84; acknowledged 15 July 1881; privy examination by McKnight, a half brother of A. M. Alexander; registered Sept 1882; Rebecca Alexander died 11 Nov 1882
verbatim_quotation: The 640 Acre Tract of land was conveyed by deed to D Travis for the Consideration of $6400.00 to be paid in three equal payments Augst 1882, 83, 84 – It was not dated but that is obviated by the date of the acknowledgement before the Clerk July 15–1881, by A. M. Alexander – on the same day a Commission was issued by the Clerk to D. M. McKnight a Justice of the Peace and a half brother of A. M. Alexander to take the Privy Examination of Mrs Alexander ... This deed was registered Sept, 1882, and she died Nov, 11 1882,

subject: Lewis Jetton; Mary Douglas; Cynthia Orr
statement: Envelope from Lewis Jetton to Mrs Mary Douglas or Cynthia Orr, Redoake; slip calls them sisters-in-law; letter addressed 'My Sisters [[Cinty?]] & Mary'
verbatim_quotation: From Lewis Jetton / Mrs Mary Douglas / or Cynthia Orr / Redoake / Texas ... To Mrs. Douglas & Cynthia Orr (sisters-in law of / From Lewis Jetton / Feb. 12, 1883 ... My Sisters [[Cinty?]] & Mary – ... L Jetton / The above you must keep in secrecy in the family

subject: L Jetton; Dr. Dickson; A. M. Alexander
statement: Lillard 'too fast'; Alexander wants no suit; 'A. M. A will do right'
verbatim_quotation: I learn from Dr. Dickson to day that Mr Alexander dont want any Suit that if there be no will he will do any thing that is right ... I believe A. M. A will do right – he has always been a Cleaver Man

subject: J. N. Spence; Mrs Bivins; A. M. Alexander
statement: Spence, son-in-law of Mrs Bivins: Alexander will give up the lands if no will; Rebecca's father on his death bed said he made no will
verbatim_quotation: P. S. J. N. Spence the soninlaw of Mrs Bivins informed me that Mr A. M. Alexander about two weeks ago said that if they found no will that he did not want any lawsuit ... she said that her Father on his death bed told her that he made no will, and asked her to promise the same and that she said that she had so promised and that she did not want Mr Alexander's kin to have her property

subject: L. A. Jetton; Susanna (Sue) Bell

verbatim_quotation: To Mrs. Susanna (Sue) / Bell / from Cousin / L. A. Jetton / (Lewis?) / Readyville, Tenn. / Feb. 20, 1870 / (Tells of death of Polly Wright)

subject: L A Jetton
statement: Very sick; Dr. Briges; Aunt Clark; Legislature to adjourn by 15 March; Sallie Wieden has had three [[Divorces?]]; John's wife has another boy
verbatim_quotation: Dr. Briges who Attend me during my sickness Thinks My illness was brought on by cold ... Aunt Clark has been with us several days ... It is Thought The Legislature will Adjurn by the 15th of march ... Sallie Wieden ... She tells us that She has had Three [[Divorces?]] but is as lively as a cricket ... Johns wife has another fine boy Three weeks old

subject: Old Aunt Polly Wright
statement: Died about two weeks before 20 Feb 1870
verbatim_quotation: Old Aunt Polly Wright died about two weeks ago She died I suppose with old age

subject: Sarah (Tullison); Smith (Popley); [[Temith?]]; Marier ([[Darnum?]] [[Vaught?]]); [[Shonce?]]; Mary; Joseph; Mr Akers; Aunt Jane
statement: 'The girls' and whom they married
verbatim_quotation: Sarah married a drunken trifling fellow by the name of Tullison They have been married fifteen years and have eight living children ... Smith Married a man name Popley ... Marier is the looking and the smartest one of the family She married [[Darnum?]] [[Vaught?]] he was killed shortly after we came here in a drunken spree ... Mary is still Single ... Joseph is married and lives in the city ... Mr Akers Says about his [[Soninlaw?]] he Says The devil owed him a grudge and has paid him off in Soninlaws ... Aunt Jane also looks very old

subject: Pap; Ellen; Cousin Ellen
statement: L A Jetton's Pap complains of poverty; love to Ellen
verbatim_quotation: Pap is always Complaining about his poverty and That he has a hard way to get along and he is afraid he will come to Starvation ... tell Ellen to write to Mary Give my love to Cousin Ellen

subject: Jesse Douglas
statement: Cross Creek, Travis County; flood; sickness; tried to rent nearer Austin; dissatisfied with the Mountains; had determined to move to Arkansas but mother-in-law's tears prevent
verbatim_quotation: Cross Creek Travis Texas / August the 30th 1869 ... I was fully determined to move to Arkansas this fall. But I must Confess that the grief and tears of a good Old motherinlaw is a preventative, at least as long as She lives and possibly She may out live Me.

subject: Earl Stewart Douglas
statement: Born 2 Aug 1869 weighing ten pounds; [[Ma?]] up two weeks
verbatim_quotation: tell Tom and Laura that Dubly Beats Me, But I must say that on the second of August Earl Stewart Douglas made his appearance Weighing ten pounds he is growing finely and [[Ma?]] has been up two weeks doing her work.

subject: Jesse Douglas
statement: Crops 1869: grass total loss, corn half rotten, cotton a third; 300 bushels sound corn; will make about 1 bag of cotton; McCluer picked 5-6 thousand off eight acres
verbatim_quotation: My grass was a total loss; corn ½ rotten my Cotton I thought at first was not injured But time tells it, I think maybe one third of a crop ... Will make or have 300 hundred Bushels sound Corn to My Share ... I fear from the progress of my Cotton in the way of its opening I wont make more than 1 Bag. McCluer off of about Eight Acres has already picked Between 5 and 6 Thousand

verbatim_quotation: Well My [[lost: torn edge]]rop amounted to one Bale [[lost: torn edge]] 434 lbs which paid My debts [[lost: torn edge]] Left me one dollar, the sale and [[lost: torn edge]]ttlement previous to sickness — [[lost: torn edge]] medicine & Dr Bill since Leaves Me about thirty dollars Behind, that I will be able to settle with the sale of Pork this winter

verbatim_quotation: It is out of the question Me to move during the Old Stewarts life time I think She would go crasy. She is old and frail in body and mind ... As I Cant Mo[[lost: torn edge]] from this Country I will Leave [[lost: torn edge]] to make your figures In regard the Old Farm

verbatim_quotation: Well I have made an investment in the way of Land for Sarahs Benefit 320 Acres lying on Kickapoo Creek in Hood County the Title to be transfered about the 20th of this month ... the above Costing Me My Noble Animal Billy Capshaw — doubt Mcdonalds [[deleted: illegible]] Selim Superior ... subject: Willie; Mary Lee; Granville; Pap; Adele; Bro Mcguffy; Jennie; Aunt Sallie
statement: L. A. Jetton's household 1883: Willie; Mary Lee's babe Granville sick; Pap improved; Adele's new home; Bro Mcguffy moved; Jennie half a mile; Aunt Sallie in West Tenn.
verbatim_quotation: Willie & myself are both as well as usual ... Mary Lees Babe little Granville has been very sick but is better to day Paps health has improved ... Adele spent Several days with me last week ... Bro Mcguffy has moved to his new home ... I am very glad to have Jennie So near me it is only a half a mile ... Aunt Sallie is still in west Tenn

subject: L. A. Jetton
statement: Lonely 'only a little negro with me'; Willie works his grandpa's land and hauls
verbatim_quotation: I have Such a lonely time here only a little negro with me Willie is at home of nights but gone every day he is working land over at his Gran Paps this year

subject: Cousin Rebecca Alexander
statement: Death from cold caught looking at the comet; in her right mind; died the evening after eating breakfast
verbatim_quotation: She exposed herself getting up very early of mornings to look at the Comet which She was very much interested about She took a very Severe Cold and died from the effect of it I think She was in her right mind all the time during her Sickness Sat up eat her breakfast and talked with her friends in the morning and died that evening

subject: Cousin Andy (A. M. Alexander); Charlie; Pap
statement: Will stolen from her drawer two weeks before her death; Andy willing to give up the land, wants to buy from the heirs; Jacob Wright estate worth about $[[26000?]]
verbatim_quotation: he told them Cousin Rebecca will was stolen out of her draw two weeks before her death he is willing to give up the land does not wish to have a law Suit but wants to buy the land of the heirs has already made arangements to get the interest of Several of the Wright family The Jacob Wright Estate is said to be worth about $[[26000?]] and my own opinion is the heirs ought to have it as Cousin Andy will be a rich man without it

subject: L. A. Jetton; Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slip: March 3 1878, mentions death[?] of Susanna Douglas Bell
verbatim_quotation: To Miss Lizzie / Douglas / from Cousin / L. A. Jetton / Readyville, Tenn / March 3, 1878 / (mentions death[?] / of Susanna Douglas bell)

subject: L. A. Jetton household 1878
statement: Pap & Mother complaining; children have whooping cough; Willie bilious fever; Adele; Cousin Nellie; Charles's children; wedding and reception at Cousin Miriam's; Jimmie & Mary; newhope church
verbatim_quotation: Pap & Mother are both Complaining and the Children all have the Whooping Cough ... Well the wedding Came off at the appointed time ... Adele Willie and myself all went to the reception At Cousin Miriams ... Jimmie & Mary are going to live with Cousin Miriam ... they have [[inserted: gone]] to Church to day at newhope

subject: Cousin Sue (Susanna Bell)
statement: Condolence: 'I loved Cousin Sue on earth I hope to meet her in heaven'
verbatim_quotation: Dear Cousin you have my deepest sympathy in your great afflictions I loved Cousin Sue on earth I hope to meet her in heaven where Sorrows and partings are unknown

subject: may beth; uncle Jimmy; Cousin S; Adele
statement: Jimmie chosen 'in fun' as son-in-law; uncle Jimmy to get pictures
verbatim_quotation: I told may beth I had picked him out for my Soninlaw (just in fun you know) ... Tell uncle Jimmy Mary is going to write to him before long and Send him hers & Jimmies pictures ... Adele says tell [[Cousin S he?]] will write to her

subject: Maybel ? Jetton; Lizzie Douglas

verbatim_quotation: To / Lizzie Douglas / from / Maybel ? / Jetton / Readyville, Tenn / Apr. 8, 1874 ... Yours Truly / [[Maybey?]] / Jetton

subject: aunt Nellie; aunt Sarah; uncle Charlie; uncle Tip; Grandpap; Mr. Barr; Nannie Fletcher; Dr. Dickson; aunt Jane
statement: Readyville kin 1874; uncle Charlie weighs 200 pounds; Mr. Barr's youngest son to marry Miss Nannie Fletcher, niece of Dr. Dickson
verbatim_quotation: aunt Nellie. She has been very sick ... She is afraid she has the consumption. aunt Sarah was over a few days ago ... uncle Charlie has grown / to be so large I dont expect you would hardly know him he weighs two hundred pounds. uncle Tip Started to Nashville for his new Spring goods last monday. Grandpap went with him ... Mr. Barrs youngest Son is to be married to morrow night to Miss Nannie Fletcher neice of Dr. Dicksons ... I suppose aunt Jane and Mr. Barr will be very well pleased

subject: new hope Church; Ma; uncle Albert
statement: Preaching first Sunday monthly; Sunday School every Sunday evening; Ma and uncle Albert teachers; church members dancing
verbatim_quotation: Several of our church members have been / dancing. We have preaching at new hope Church the first Sunday in every month and Sunday School every Sunday evening. Ma and uncle Albert are teachers

subject: Jennie White Jetton; Delie; Willie; Joanna; Cousin George
statement: Children at school; scrapbook; asks Cousin George for verses
verbatim_quotation: Little Jennie White Jetton is Staying [[deleted: here]] going to school. She and Delie have a fine time to gether ... Joanna has had her [[deleted: illegible]] flower garden made ... I have Started me a Scrapbook tell Cousin George to Send me some pretty verses to

subject: Maybel/Marybee Jetton
statement: Longs to see 'my old home and friends' (i.e. Texas)
verbatim_quotation: Dear cousin you dont know how much I should like to see my old home and friends once more. I thought when I first came away I could soon forget you all; but not so

subject: L A Jetton (Lewis ?); Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slip: to Miss Lizzie Douglas from Cousin L A Jetton (Lewis ?), Readyville
verbatim_quotation: To Miss Lizzie / Douglas / from Cousin / L A Jetton / (Lewis ?) / Readyville, Tenn. / Feb 1, 1874

subject: Readyville school; Bro Rice Sewell; newhope
statement: School taught by a preaching brother; Bro Rice Sewell preaches at newhope once a month; three other churches
verbatim_quotation: The school will be taught at Readyville by one of our preaching brethren he has been teaching for many years and is a Splendid scholar and a good man We have preaching at newhope once a month Bro Rice Sewell preaches for us again this year

subject: Lizzie Douglas; L A Jetton
statement: Lizzie sent money from her Ma's sale of the saddle
verbatim_quotation: I was very much surprised when I saw the Money you sent me I never dreamed of such a thing as your Ma selling the saddle but as you say money never comes amiss

subject: Mr Barr; Aunt Jane; Marybee; Charlie; Alma; Eddie Jolly; Emma; Peter
statement: Readyville kin, 1874; Charlie's wife disliked; Eddie Jolly courting Marybee
verbatim_quotation: Mr Barr and Aunt Jane Came up and Spent a night with us ... Marybee went to Readyville last week and [[deleted: illegible]] her picture taken ... Charlie and family are all getting on finely Little Alma is a sweet little thing ... I have less use for his lady than any woman I ever saw ... Mr Eddie Jolly one of Emmas brothers is coming to see Marybee I dont know what Peter will say about it

subject: Fannie (Columbia Goodloe); Tommie, French, Bobbie, Mary; Newton Goodloe; Mary Douglas; Cynthia Orr
