verbatim_quotation: To Cousin / Lizzie Douglas / from / Fannie ? / (Columbia Goodloe) / Mentions in letter / brothers Tommie / (Thomas), French, / Bobbie (Robert), sister / Mary – children / of Newton Goodloe, / the brother of Mary / Douglas & Cynthia Orr / Written from / Russellville, Ala. / June 21, 1874

subject: Fannie; Uncle Dr Clarke; Uncle John; Brother French; Russell; Eugene; Broth Tommie; little N L; Broth Bobbie; Sis Mary; Pa
statement: Fannie keeps house for Uncle Dr Clarke (widower, 5 children); Uncle John; will live with Brother French; Tommie's children incl. 'little N L'; Bobbie in the drug store; Sis Mary weighs 84
verbatim_quotation: I am now staying with my Uncle Dr Clarke he has very recently lost his wife and he has 5 little Children ... Uncle John is very anxious for me to live with him ... dear Brother French has always done so much for me ... he has two Beautiful Boys Russell and Eugene Broth Tommie has 2 [[illegible]] and little N L Broth Bobbie is with Broth French in the Drug store Sis Mary lives 2 miles from here her health is very bad now ... only weighs 84 I weigh 125

subject: Fannie's Pa (Newton Goodloe per slip)
statement: Pa is in Texas and pleased; hoped he will stay with Lizzie's family or Aunt Cynthia
verbatim_quotation: I am glad Pa is so much pleased with Texas I hope he can get business out there I wish Brother would move out there too I hope Pa will stay with you all or Aunt Cynthia one ... Tell Pa I am anxiously awaiting an answer to my letter ... Your Unknown but loving Cousin / Fannie

subject: Lizzie Graves; Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slips call Lizzie Graves 'Aunt' and 'Miss'; one slip 'Written by Miss Lizzie Graves To Aunt Lizzie'
verbatim_quotation: To Lizzie Douglas ? / from / Lizzie Graves ... Written by Miss Lizzie Graves / To Aunt Lizzie ... To Lizzie Douglas / from Aunt / [Miss Lizzie Graves] / Pratties Ala.

subject: Lizzie Graves; Bud Joe; Bud Davy; Charlie; Pa
statement: Bud Joe to Mobile hoping to join an emigrating company for Brazil; Pa planted ~50 acres corn; three hundred acres to cultivate; Snowden
verbatim_quotation: Pa and Bud Joe went to Snowden to day (about fifteen miles from here) ... there is an emigrating company to start from there to Brazil between the 15th & 20th of this Month he wants to get with them if he doesnt succeed in that he may land in Texas ... Bud Davy has gotten shut of the chills ... I dont know how much corn Pa has planted about fifty acres I reckon ... We have / three hundred acres to cultivate

subject: Parson Bone; Mr. Rouse; Ellen Douglas; Sue Roberts; Mollie
statement: Valentines and 'Flora'; Ellen Douglas has Flora
verbatim_quotation: I suppose you could not afford to go and let Parson Bone make jewely of you ... Ellen Douglas have Flora but I dont know that the emblems are all the same ... I wrote to Sue Roberts not long ago ... I wrote to Mollie not long ago

subject: Grand ma; Bud John; Aunt Jane (Jenny's own mother); Uncle J.
statement: Aunt Jane's family to move in; her husband and two daughters to California
verbatim_quotation: Aunt Jane and her family (Jennys own mother) expect to move out in a few weeks. her husband and two of her daughters and their families have gone to California Uncle J. has only gone to look at the country

subject: Lizzie Graves
statement: New saddle, gloves, pony that kneels; Pa's eyes worse
verbatim_quotation: I have a new saddle and new gloves and a little pony that will kneel for me to get on ... Pas eyes are getting worse

subject: Lizzie Graves
statement: Pratville Ala.; home named Mosshead or Buttonwood Hall
verbatim_quotation: Pratville Ala. / Sunday evening March 10 67 ... The name of our present home is Mosshead or Button wood hall

subject: Lizzie Graves; Laura
statement: Laura going away so far; regards to Lizzie's father and Mother and Mr [[Orr?]]
verbatim_quotation: I am sorry for you that Laura is going away so far from you remember me very kindly to her when you see her my kindest regards your father and Mother also to Mr [[Orr?]]

subject: Lizzie Graves
statement: Would rather live in Texas; Pa moved to Alabama for Grand Ma and schooling; cannot go to school; sewing
verbatim_quotation: it is true I would much rather live in Texas and I sometimes feel right sad when I think about having left there ... Grand Ma living here alone She has only one other Son ... thinking as he did that the opportunities for schooling [[inserted: us]] would be greater than to have stayed there

subject: Cousin [[M. W.?]]; Mrs. G's little girl
statement: Three corpses at one sight; Cousin M. W. left eight children, six girls, oldest boy about sixteen gone to Virginia
verbatim_quotation: About a month ago I saw something that I never witnessed before—three corpses at one sight all to be laid in one family grave yard Cousin [[M. W.?]] and her little infant were laid in one coffin and Mrs. G's little girl in another ... Cousin M. left [[inserted: eight]] children—[[two?]] grown live / less, six girls, the oldest in her fifteenth year The oldest boy (about sixteen) left home a few days before her death for Virginia to go to school

subject: Lizzie Graves; Miss Mattie B.; Mr. C.
statement: Sunday School class of seven boys; gave a boy a Bible; lessons historical, Abraham to David
verbatim_quotation: I have a class in Sunday School composed of seven boys ... he said they did not have a Bible in the family so I gave him a Bible ... We dont use any book in the class but the Bible the lessons we teach now are all historical

subject: Annie Roberts; Frank; Bud Davy; Bud Joe
statement: Chills; Frank sick; Bud Joe overseer four miles off
verbatim_quotation: you and Annie Roberts have been more punctual than any of my correspondents ... Frank and I both took chills ... Bud Joe has had one & I dont know he is not at home now he is living about four miles from here hiring as overseer for one of our Cousins until the cotton crop is gathered

subject: Lizzie Graves
statement: Fruit in Alabama: no peaches; Grand Ma's orchard destroyed by a tornado; pomegranate trees
verbatim_quotation: I do want some good peaches so bad haven't had any here since I left home ... she once had an apple and pear orchard [[illegible]] it was destroyed a few years ago by a tornado that blew her house down ... Grand Ma has plenty of pomegranate trees did you ever see any?

subject: Lizzie Graves; Grand Ma; Pa; Frank; Episcopalians; Methodists
statement: Kin nearly all Methodists; Pa and one sister 'gone astray'; protracted Methodist meeting suspended for election days; Frank reading the Bible
verbatim_quotation: Lizzie I thought I had told you that our kin were nearly all Methodists ... Pa and one of his sisters have gone astray from the teachings of their childhood my Aunt is a member of the Episcopal Church ... the meeting is suspended untill wednesday on account of today and tomorrow being election days ... Frank has been reading the Bible a good deal lately I do wish we had a good preacher I think his mind is now open to receive the truth ... I think Grand Ma [[tries?]] hopes to win us all over to the Methodist church

subject: Lizzie Graves; Mr. — ('my beau')
statement: Evening ride to a persimmon tree; 'he doesn't suit my style'
verbatim_quotation: Mr. — ("my beau") was there, he asked me to take a ride with [[inserted: him]] and Oh! we had a "[[time of it?]]!" rode on horse back we went to a persimmon tree ... he is a very nice young man but he doesn't "suit my style" so much of my nonsense

subject: Pa (Graves); Montgomery; Lowndes
statement: Pa to Montgomery and Lowndes; crops tolerably good
verbatim_quotation: Crops are tolerably good here corn is turning out pretty well Cotton better than I expected ... Pa went to Montgomery [[deleted: illegible]] [[inserted: to day]] Tuesday ... he expects to go to Lowndes tomorrow

subject: Lizzie Graves
statement: Sick in bed nearly a week; 'an Ala. girl' (pale faces)
verbatim_quotation: My sickness has served to make me look like an Ala. girl the first morning that I was able to fill my seat at the table some of them said "Cousin Lizzie your sickness shows right smartly on you" I said "Oh! it is only helping to make an Ala. girl of me" ... "we dont have as many pale faces there as you do here"

subject: Lizzie Graves; Pa; Mr. Thurgeson; Christian Church; Liberty
statement: Heard of a Christian church twelve or fifteen miles south; Pa and she 'alone'; 'series of doctrinal sermons like they do at Liberty'
verbatim_quotation: Pa heard of a christian Church some twelve or fifteen miles south of this ... I havnt met up with any one yet who is a member of the Christian Church Pa and I are alone it makes me feel right badly ... we dont have series of doctrinal sermons like they do at Liberty

subject: Mr. Ba; Mr. Horns; Mr. Goodman; Mr. Austin; Jane and Mary; Aunt Susanna Andrews (Graves)
statement: Examinations; Mr. Goodman moving; letter enclosed for Jane and Mary ('the boys'); storm reported by Aunt Susanna Andrews (Graves)
verbatim_quotation: I wish very much I could have been with you at Mr. Ba's examination ... Lizzie do you ever hear anything from Mr. Goodman these days poor man I reckon he will move and move until he settle in his grave ... Where is Mr. Austin ... I have written a letter to Jane and Mary which I hope you will pardon me for sending in yours give it to any of or all the boys and they will get some person to read it for them ... I received a letter from Aunt Susanna Andrews (Graves) a few days ago

subject: Lizzie Graves; Dr. (L. Douglas) & Ellen
statement: Slip: May 10 1867, regards given to Dr. (L. Douglas) & Ellen; letter gives regards 'to the Dr. and Ellen also to Maggy and Jennie Bell'
verbatim_quotation: (Regards given to Dr. (L. Douglas) / & Ellen. ... Give my kind regards to the Dr. and Ellen also to Maggy and Jennie Bell and to all enquiring friends ... L. J. G.

subject: Lizzie Graves
statement: Pa's sore eyes; chills broken with red pepper; brothers Frank, [[Thaddie?]] & Charles at work
verbatim_quotation: he has had sore eyes very bad but they are improving now I very much feared he would entirely lose one of them ... had two or three chills but broke them up with red pepper / I have been quite well since then Brothers are now at work trying to earn their bread by the sweat of their brow work seems to agree with Frank [[Thaddie?]] & Charles

subject: Memorial decorations, Alabama 1867
statement: May party at Tusk[egee?] to decorate Confederate graves; the colored ladies of Montgomery decorated the Yankee dead; Methodist reunion convention; Catholics
verbatim_quotation: There was a May party given by the ladies at Tusk[[illegible]] the first of this month ... to decorate the graves of the Alabama confederate dead A few days after the white ladies had enjoyed their [[deleted: illegible]] on the confederate dead The colored ladies of the city of Montgomery formed a procession marched down to the graveyard loaded with flowers to decorate the graves of the Yankee dead ... The church convention is now in [[illegible]] for the purpose of uniting the Methodist Episcopal and Methodist Protestant churches again ... The Catholics have been making quite a [[illegible]] here lately

subject: Corn price
statement: Corn selling at $2.00 per bushel (Alabama, May 1867)
verbatim_quotation: he is going to carry corn off for sale it is selling at $2.00 per bushel

subject: Lizzie Graves; Uncle J.; Aunt; Cousin Mary
statement: Uncle returned from California delighted; cousins moved to Los Angeles; earthquakes; bought a home in Greenville thirty miles off; beaus
verbatim_quotation: My Uncle has returned from California highly delighted with every thing ... Sanfrancisco is far a head of Montgomery in the fashions if not ahead of New York ... My cousins found it too gay for them, so they moved about 500 five hundred miles south of that to Los angeles ... I think the Earth quakes they have been having out there have shaken his determination ... he has bought a home in Greenville, about thirty miles from here ... We have been having a good many "beaus" since Cousin M. came

subject: Mr Winniford's marriage
statement: Lizzie Graves has not heard of Mr Winnifords marriage; sympathizes with Lizzie's loneliness
verbatim_quotation: I have not heard of Mr Winnifords marriage I know how to sympathize with you in your loneliness

subject: M E Goodloe; Lizzie Douglas
statement: Slip: to Lizzie Douglas from (Niece) M E Goodloe, Randolph (Field); letter addresses Lizzie as 'Dear Niece'
verbatim_quotation: To Lizzie Douglas / from (Niece) / M E Goodloe / Randolph – (Field) / Feb 12, 1865 ... Randolph Feb the 12 1865 / Miss Lizzie D. / Dear Niece

subject: Henry Orr
statement: Passing through on his way to his command two days' ride away; five weeks from his command, detained in Louisiana with a lame horse
verbatim_quotation: I was allso agreable surprised in a viset from Henry Orr the other day he was passing thru this Co on his way to his command which is in two days ride of this plaise he only staid too nights with us he was well He has not ben withe the command in 5 weeks he was ditained in Luisiana on the account of his horse being lame

subject: Uncle Tom; Granvill and Babe; Nannie; Mary Orr; Laura; Sue
statement: M E Goodloe's kin; party with supper and dance; 'my brittest hopes have been blasted'
verbatim_quotation: I was at Uncle Toms when he came we wer just starting to a party ... I did justice to the Supper but of cours tuck no hands in the dance ... Lizzie I do not think their is any more purfict happiness in this world for me for my brittest hopes have been blasted ... I heard from Granvill and Babe the other day ... Nannie is bothering me ... Tell Mary Orr that I think it time that she had answered my letter tell Laura ... tell Sue to write to me

subject: M E Goodloe; George Douglas
statement: Received a letter from George Douglas and answered it; 'old Houston'
verbatim_quotation: I received a letter from George Douglas and answered it and think it time that I was getting a nother one / Lizzie their is some very pretty girls and boys in old Houston

subject: Mrs [[Stinnet?]] (Claunch) murder
statement: Sisters' account: Mrs [[S?]] killed; daughter Mollie aged 15 suspected; girl's bloody dress found; bond of [[five?]] hundred dollars; jailed at [[Wax?]]; Mrs Douglas first on the scene
verbatim_quotation: I have a horrible tale to recount this week tis the murder of Mrs [[Stinnet?]] by her daughter. Mrs [[S?]] is a sister to Mr [[Simons?]] ... Mrs Douglas was the first one to get there after it happened, and [[illegible]] poor crying little child & asked it who kilt her Mother – [[illegible]] the child said it was Mollie. Search was made and the girls dress was found concealed, all bloody. ... three days was given her to give [[five?]] hundred dollars bond she could not so her [[illegible]] went to [[Wax?]] jail.

subject: Sister; Pleas Tyler; John; [[Morriss?]]; Mr [[Morton?]]
statement: Laura's Friday Sept 18 page; Sister's children
verbatim_quotation: Sisters children came home with me this morning she came this evening They are all well and hearty Sister is quite uneasy about her [[beef?]] ... Pleas Tyler is [[illegible]] and I heard him say he would be gone about ten days

subject: Lizzie (to George)
statement: Bought a saddle for twelve dollars; packing something for 'you boys'
verbatim_quotation: I have got me a beautiful saddle got it [[illegible]] Mrs [[illegible]] brought it [[illegible]] twelve dollars

subject: Magruder; flour speculation
statement: Wheat carried in before the tithe tax sold by speculators; man from Nacochitoches says Magruder is at the head of it; sending George a sack of flour and fat bacon for his fish
verbatim_quotation: It is now currently reported and believed, that the wheat which the Farmers carried in before the tythe tax, was due, in order that the Soldiers might get some flour has been sold by speculators. ... There was a man here the other day from Nacochitoches who says this is so, and that Magruder is at the head of it. ... What if old Magruder orders you away from Sabine about the time Joda gets back, and takes all of your flour and bacon away from you? We are going to send you a sack of flour a piece and a good supply of fat bacon which I hope will serve to make your fish a little more savory.

subject: Joda; Mr Banks; Col. [[illegible]]
statement: Joda saw Mr Banks in Dallas; bridle cannot be got; blanket mended
verbatim_quotation: Joda saw Mr Banks in Dallas the last day he was there ... We will send all the things required, without it is the bridle. ... I have finished mending your blanket.

subject: Joda; Velasco; Dock; J. M.; Mr Bell
statement: Joda arrived 18 April 1865; George returned from Velasco; thread sent by J. M.; flour speculation (600 lbs) to send by Joda; side saddle for Laura from Houston
verbatim_quotation: We were somewhat surprised last tuesday evening — the 18th by the arrival of Joda ... suppose you have written by mail since your return from Velasco. I am anxious to hear something about Dock ... The thread you sent by J. M. was very acceptable, it will save me many a turn of my "Piano." ... It is to send down some flour by Joda that Laura and I have. There is only six hundred pounds of it ... I would like for you to look around a little, and see if a side saddle could be got in Houston. Laura is very anxious to get one

subject: Laura
statement: Teaching school away from home, 16 to 19 scholars
verbatim_quotation: I recd a letter from Laura this evening. she seems to be very well satisfied in her new situation. says she has from 16 to 19 schollars, with a prospect for more. I suppose it is better than to be carding and spinning

subject: Cousin Mollie; Mrs. Bishop; May; Kirkham
statement: Cousin Mollie at school at Liberty; Mrs. Bishop from Dallas teaching there
verbatim_quotation: She is going to Liberty; A mrs. Bishop is teaching there now. She is from Dallas ... could teach almost every thing the Dead Languages included. But May says it is with difficulty she can find the answers in old Kirkham

subject: Stiles boys; Stanley; Jim Floyd; Mrs Campbell; Jennie Bell
statement: Horse theft; deserter Stiles boys; one hung on the limb Stanley was hung on; party of 8 or 10 men; 'I dread the consequences of this mob law'
verbatim_quotation: Several horses have been stolen, and two Stiles boys who lived over in the neck and were deserters, were suspected. A company of men got after them, and caught one of them — the Youngest; he acknowledged to stealing and said his brother was concerned in it. They hung him on the same limb Stanley was hung on — so we have heard. ... Last Sunday morning a party of 8 or 10 men passed Mrs Campbells — aunt [[Bats?]] house — with one of the Stileses. Jim Floyd was one of the party. ... Perhaps they merited death, but I dread the consequences of this mob law. We know not, but this is the beginning of terrible times. I hate the thought that Brushy should be the place of the beginning of such things.

subject: [[Foythe?]] (Fayette); Bob
statement: Fayette not returned; Bob chills, seeking furlough
verbatim_quotation: [[Foythe?]] has not yet returned; the last news from them, Bob was having the chills, and was trying to get a furlough to come with F.

subject: Henry and Ellen; Father
statement: Henry and Ellen went up (home) last Wednesday; Henry helped Father sow grass seed; stove set up; well cleaned
verbatim_quotation: Henry and Ellen went up last wednesday, so we are once more by our selves. Henry helped Father to sow his grass seed before he went away. They have got the stove set up ... They got the top of the well, a good many old shoes and large rocks and a Young possum out of the well.

subject: brother Methodist Jones; Liberty
statement: Will hold forth at Liberty; Lizzie has not heard a discourse since 1 March
verbatim_quotation: Tomorrow, brother Methodist Jones, will hold forth at Liberty. I will try to attend as I have not heard a discourse since the 1st of March.

subject: Joda; [[Fran?]]; Warren
statement: Joda at home plowing; two letters from [[Fran?]] dated 26 March; love to Warren
verbatim_quotation: Joda says tell you he is at home safe, and a plowing. ... We recd two letters from [[Fran?]], last dated 26th of March. He is very anxious to come home ... With best love to Warren and yourself I remain Lizzie

subject: Jeppe; Mr Rutherford; Mary Burkhead; Theodore Wylie; Miss Mattie; Sis
statement: Jeppe bought Laura's pony going to San Antonio; nag bought from Mr Rutherford; George's 'almost rude word' to Sis
verbatim_quotation: Jeppe bought Laura's pony when he went to San Antonio I consider him a poor horse ... You say "Sis sends her respects to me, ask her what I must do with them." ... we bought her from Mr Rutherford, father of the one that married Mary Burkhead; If you remember, Mr Rutherford bought out Theodore Wylies; and by the by he has a daughter just "Sweet Sixteen" Miss Mattie

subject: Lizzie to George
statement: Advice on George's handwriting and spelling; letters marked 'Due ten cents'
verbatim_quotation: I know you know how to spell, but you sometimes leave out letters, which causes [[deleted: them]] [[inserted: words]] to be spelt wrong. ... your letters are sometimes marked "Due ten cents".

subject: Mr Graves; Thos; Joe
statement: Joe taken prisoner and paroled by the Feds
verbatim_quotation: March 20th all well today Mr Graves Thos Uncle came over to work this morning they say Joe has got home he was taken prisner and Paroled by the Feds.

subject: Mr. Graves; Dolpheus; Laura
statement: Laura's fragment: Mr. Graves planting corn; the boy whose hand was mashed off
verbatim_quotation: Thursday 28. Mr. Graves commenced planting corn ... I did not send one by Dolpheus / In your next give us the name of the Boy that got his hand mashed off. ... Affectionately / Laura

subject: Battle below Shreveport
statement: Fragment: fight below Shreveport, two thousand prisoners; slip says Reb capture of 2000 prisoners
verbatim_quotation: — Tells of battle / below Shreveport — / with Reb capture of / 2000 prisoners ... 17th We [[illegible]] just [[illegible]] us [[illegible]] fight below Shreveport. [[illegible]] says we [[illegible]] two thousand prisoners, five [[illegible]]. [[deleted: cannon]] [[illegible]] forty

subject: Sunday school
statement: Sunday school commences today; 'all well on Brushy'
verbatim_quotation: Sunday school commences to day I dont expect to attend much. This leaves all well on Brushy.

subject: Laura (per slip) to George
statement: Slip: Feb. 11, 1865(?); letter dated Feb 1st 1865 'By the fire Sandy'; run on Blazes leading Jenney; spinning; Lizzie & Jeannie deserted us
verbatim_quotation: By the fire Sandy / [[illegible]] Feb 1st / 1865 / Dear George ... I had quite a run on Blazes leading Jenney ... Spinning is my constant employmen at home ... Lizzie & Jeannie have entire deserted us ... Keep out of mischief dont forget [[how Lol?]]

subject: Lizzie to George, letter No. 8
statement: Brushy, Thursday night April 14 1864; the Dr.; all well on Hack except Joe; Jeppe coming down; Beck and [[Wash?]] from Grape Vine Springs because water is scarce; Ellen wants to [[sell?]] out and move to this neighborhood; militia service ten days out of forty; deserters at [[Tyler?]]; Mrs White presented a six shooter
verbatim_quotation: No. 8 / Brushy Texas / Thursday night April 14th 1864 / Dear brother — ... They were all well on Hack except Joe ... Jeppe will be coming down [[illegible]] here now. Beck and [[Wash?]] have had to come [[illegible]] from Grape Vine Springs. On account of water being so scarce ... They only have to [[illegible]] ten days out of every forty. He thinks if he [[illegible]] Ellen he will be exempt on account of [[illegible]] militia. ... Mrs White presented a six shooter and told them if they advanced she would shoot them. so they did not take Mr White. Hurrah! for some of the women dont you say so.

subject: Joda; Watts; Ingeville; Johnson; John Turney
statement: Turkey hunting; pet deer; panther; six mule team
verbatim_quotation: [[Colburn?]] came to stay all night to go a turkey hunting with Joda in the morning, but was disappointed as Joda went to Dallas to day to see Watts having failed to see him at Ingeville as he went to Johnson ... You ought to be here to hear the turkeys gobble of a morning and see some of our beautiful pet deer. ... which [[illegible]] we suppose to be a panther. ... On the subject of John Turneys, the people of [[Tennessee?]] are anxious that he shall get a six mule team

subject: Genl McCullough; William Duff; Jno Smith; Rome
statement: Peace questions; the cotton trade; McCullough's rendezvous trap capturing 200 men; Rome to Wax. seeking to drive a team San Antonio to Eagle Pass
verbatim_quotation: You say dont get too fast on the peace questions I will not, for I never was as sanguine as Father and [[Louisa?]] ... But I always have and always will think there is something wrong about this cotton trade. ... Genl McCullough ... two hundred of them had arrived when they were surrounded by a Regmt and taken prisoners ... [[deleted: among them William Duff and his]] nephews Jno Smith who have returned to this section ... Rome has now gone to Wax. with a waggon master ... to try to get to drive a team from San Antonio to Eagle Pass.

subject: Lizzie Douglas; George Douglas
statement: Slip: Nov. 13, 1864; mentions Henry & Ellen's safe return, prisoners at Tyler, plastic surgery
verbatim_quotation: To George Douglas / from / Lizzie Douglas / Nov. 13, 1864 / — / mentions Henry & / Ellen Douglas safe / return. / Speaks of prisoners at / Tyler, Tex. / Tells of plastic surgery

subject: Liberty; Mrs Justin's funeral; Haynes, Justin, Maley, White, Berry
statement: Funeral sermon at Liberty from Hebrews 11:4, two hours, much on depreciation of the currency; the Colony; Shilo
verbatim_quotation: This morning Lou and I went to meeting to Liberty to hear Mrs Justins funeral preached; it was to have been preached at the Colony last Sunday ... Five preachers: Haynes, Justin, Maley, White, and Berry. Mr Haynes gave us a long tedious discourse from the last clause of the 4th vs. of the 11th ch. Hebrews. He spoke fully two hours, and a good portion of his sermon was about the depreciation of the currency

subject: Aunt Bettie; Betsy
statement: Aunt Bettie moved (to Arkansas) on the 10th [Nov 1864] taking Betsy and chickens
verbatim_quotation: We assisted aunt Bettie in getting ready to move ... She got off on the morning of the 10th / She took Betsy and chickens, left the spinnack and what few cows she had ... Aunt Bettie told me to tell you to write to her [[illegible]] Ark.

subject: Father (N. L. Douglas)
statement: Bought a sow and five shoats for ten dollars specie; reserved twenty acres for corn and hungarian; Gibson to raise wheat for a fourth
verbatim_quotation: Father bought a sow and five shoats from her for ten dollars specie, so I reckon we are safe in the meat line for another year ... Father has reserved twenty acres for [[corn?]] and hungarian. ... he was just to raise the wheat, cut it and thrash it and put a fourth in the granary.

subject: The well
statement: Well waters a dozen mules and horses
verbatim_quotation: The well holds out finely about a dozen mules and horses are watered out of it twice and three times a day.

subject: Old Abe; [[Childsy?]]; Mc. Clelland
statement: Lincoln's election; four more years of war feared
verbatim_quotation: If I had any hopes of the war ending soon I would feel so much better but from the tone of the papers, we need not look for peace in four more years. Old Abe is elected in all probability and [[Childsy?]] thinks it is best for if Mc. Clelland is elected says he, propositions will be made which some of the States will accept, and then we are ruined.

subject: [[Childsy?]]; Mr Grounds
statement: Soldier visitors from George's camp
verbatim_quotation: [[Childsy?]] was nearly frozen, but a warm fire soon set him to talking, and he and Mr Grounds (a soldier that came with him) kept us laughing ... you and Joda had talked so much about him

subject: Henry and Ellen; Warren; Beck; Griffin
statement: Henry and Ellen started home 8 Nov 1864; Warren expected with Beck; 'Griffin or somebody else must have a particular spite at Warren'
verbatim_quotation: Henry and Ellen started home on the 8th, all well and hearty. we have not heard from Warren but look for him and Beck down. Griffin or somebody else must have a particular spite at Warren. If he did not get his furlough lengthened, his stay at home will be short.

subject: Dock [[Wyrman?]]; Ed Dickson
statement: Dock in Co. G, Bates' Reg at Velasco; 'I am a peace man, let it come as it may'; Ed Dickson at Tyler guarding prisoners
verbatim_quotation: We recd a letter from Dock [[Wyrman?]] not long since, dated 10th Oct. He had just got Fathers letter and the socks we sent by Ed Dickson. ... He belongs to Co. G. Bates' Reg which is stationed at Velasco ... He winds up his letter by saying "I am a peace man, let it come as it may." Ed Dickson is now at Tyler guarding prisoners.

subject: [[Rome?]]; Sister
statement: Rome tells Sister to buy two more wagons and come to San Antonio in the spring
verbatim_quotation: [[Rome?]] it seems has a notion of hanging on to the service. The last letter Sister got from him he told her to buy two more waggons (a horse and an ox waggon) and come to him in the spring. Sister is mightily pleased, she has been wanting to leave here a long time. She thinks she can rent a house in San Antonio and send the children to school

subject: Jeppe; Warren; Beck
statement: Jeppe arrived 15 Nov 1864, going to San Antonio with wool; Warren cannot bring Beck; will be here 10 Dec on his way back to Sabine
verbatim_quotation: Jeppe got here yesterday he will only stay down a few days, as he is going to San Antonio with a load of wool as soon as he returns. Henry and Ellen [[inserted: had]] got back safe. Warren not got down; he can get no conveyance to bring Beck down while he stays; he wrote he would be here on the 10th of Dec. on his way back to Sabine. I suppose he got his furlough lengthened.

subject: Mr. Marshall's family; Lou's house
statement: Family from Arkansas, two sons and six daughters; 'the feds treated them better than our folks'
verbatim_quotation: On last monday Mr. Marshalls family [[deleted: was]] rolled in from Ark. composed of two sons and six daughters. ... The jayHawkers were the only ones that pestered them much. They say the feds treated them better than our folks. The old man has rented Lous house for them

subject: [[Lidda?]] Baker; Dr. Mc. [[Curdy?]]
statement: Gold nose covered with forehead skin
verbatim_quotation: As an other item of news I will tell you about [[Lidda?]] Bakers nose. Dr. Mc. [[Curdy?]] is making her a new one; he made a gold nose and then cut a piece of skin out of her forehead and twisted it around and covered the gold. ... He says he is going to make her a lip when her nose gets well and then take her for pay.

subject: Jane Green
statement: Died of pneumonia
verbatim_quotation: Jane Green died last Saturday night with pneumonia.

subject: Lizzie Douglas; George Douglas
statement: Slip: Feb. 19, 1864; mentions Jim Orr's letter, wounded at Chickamauga; deserters; Quantrill's Raiders
verbatim_quotation: To George Douglas / from Sister / Lizzie Douglas / Brushy — / Feb. 19, 1864 / [[deleted: Letter no. 4]] / mentions Jim Orr's / letter — wounded at / Chickamauga. / describes war & / Lizzie also speaks of / deserters — / Quantrills Raiders

subject: Fayette; M Orr; Jim; Tole Hamilton
statement: Letters from Fayette and Jim; Jim slightly wounded at Chickamauga; Tole Hamilton fell at Ringold
verbatim_quotation: Laura got a letter from Fayette, M Orr one from Fayette, Mary and I one apiece from Jim. / They have come safely through all the fights except the slight wound Jim rec. at Chickamauga. ... Jim says "he can stand the fatigue and hardships all very well, till it comes to the fighting fighting, and then when he sees his comrades falling around him, it is all he can do to persuade himself not to run." Tole Hamilton fell at Ringold, in the retreat. he was shot through the breast, and only lived a few minutes. ... He leaves a widow and child.

subject: Goodloes (Aquilla's sons); Squire; uncle [[Givans?]]; Charly Brown; Will; Will G.; Will Brown; Mary G.; Billy
statement: Two Goodloes deserted; Squire 'safe over the Border'; Will safe in a Northern clime
verbatim_quotation: The boys write home that two Goodloes (Aquilla's sons) have deserted. And whose name do you expect to hear [[illegible]]? Tell no other than Squire. ... But Squire is safe over the Border, where a many another poor Dixie boy wishes he was I expect. ... Charly Brown has written to them, that Will is safe with his kindred in a Northern Clime ... Mary G. is perfectly satisfied about Billy. ... He was at Chicago when Charly heard from him

subject: George's battalion; Joda; Tom [[Warthen?]]; Gurley's reg.; Murray's Texas Co.
statement: Joda thinks George's battalion disgraced; guard round Gurley's regiment; Murray's Texas Co. all left but sixteen
verbatim_quotation: From the tone of Jodas letter, he seems to think your Batt. is disgraced worse than any other body of men in the Army, but he is behind the times ... Tom [[Warthen?]] writes home that they have to keep a guard round Gurleys reg. to keep them from deserting. We hear there all of Murrays Texas Co. have left but Sixteen.

subject: Quantrill's men; [[Sherrol?]]
statement: Men in the Confederacy who murder for money; Sherrol's tales of killing union men
verbatim_quotation: I think there are men in this Confederacy, mean enough to perpetrate any and all of the crimes committed by him, and that for less motive, than Quantrills men were actuated by. ... But there are men in this confederacy who murder for money and I have some reason to believe, that [[Sherrol?]] is one of them. ... Such as going to a union man's house, passing himself off for a union man get into the others Sentiments, then draw out his pistol and shoot him down.

subject: Jim White; militia
statement: Militia armed with sticks
verbatim_quotation: Jim White says the militia [[illegible]] are armed with sticks. ... he says his command had guns as they were dismounted Cavalry, but some of them were actually armed with sticks for guns.

subject: Emmie; uncle Geo.; Cousin Mollie; Laura; baby May; Ellen
statement: Emmie asks uncle Geo. for little letters; George's poems 'We are growing old' and 'O would I were a child again'; the baby, blue-eyed little May
verbatim_quotation: I asked Emmie what to tell uncle Geo. she says tell he do write me little letters. Cousin Mollie is here to night. ... Laura wishes to know if you completed "We are growing old" and "O would I were a child again" they are beautiful verses. I never once told you a word about the baby. She is a very pretty, blue eyed fair skinned little May. ... Ellen and Emmie have grown a great deal since you left. Ellen can spin pretty well on two spindles.

subject: Lizzie; George; Lafayette Orr; Henry Orr; Cynthia; Jim Orr; Uncle Alfred
statement: Slip: June 28, 1864, Letter no. 18: Lafayette Orr prisoner of war, through Henry Orr's letter to Cynthia & Jim Orr; death of Uncle Alfred (manuscript numbered No. 13)
verbatim_quotation: — Tells of hearing from / Lafayette Orr as / prisoner of war thru / Henry Orr letter to / Cynthia & Jim Orr / — Tells of death of / Uncle Alfred ... No. 13. / Brushy, June 28th 1864.

subject: Uncle Alfred; Aunt Bettie; Mr Orr; Henry
statement: Uncle Alfred died late Sunday evening 5 June 1864, 18 days after being wounded; Aunt Bettie fainted; Mary Orr and Lizzie sat with her
verbatim_quotation: I have sorrowful news to tell you this morning. Uncle Alfred is dead. Mr Orr recd a letter from Henry yesterday, confirming what we had heard before. He died late Sunday evening the 5th of this month, just 18 days after he was wounded. Poor Aunt Bettie is allmost crushed beneath the blow. As soon as she heard it was really true, she fainted away

subject: Uncle Alfred's wound
statement: Bone fractured below the knee cap
verbatim_quotation: the bone had been considerably fractured, just below the knee cap, and upon pressing it a good deal of matter run out with the oil of the knee cap.

subject: Uncle Alf; John Morgan; Docter Gardner; Bob [[Head?]]; cousin Gran; Bob; Thos. Harper; Parsons men; Coz G
statement: 'I just want to get into one big fight, that will do me'; buried between John Morgan and Docter Gardner; Bob says he was the coolest man in the company; Parsons' men to Houston
verbatim_quotation: Poor Uncle Alf. when he told Lou and me goodbye he said "I just want to get into one big fight, that will do me." But now he sleeps between two comrades in arms — John Morgan, and [[deleted: illegible]] [[inserted: Docter]] Gardner. Bob [[Head?]] and his lady called upon us ... He says Uncle A. was a good soldier — he watched him during the fight and he appeared to be the coolest man in the Co. Henry writes that cousin Gran is able to walk some ... Thos. Harper got in the other day, he says Parsons men have been ordered to Houston.

subject: Methodists at Liberty; Parson Sansom; [[Coltr V.?]]
statement: Methodist meeting at Liberty, seats moved under the trees; dinner on the ground
verbatim_quotation: Well the Methodists are having another grand time at Liberty; their meeting commenced last Thursday night ... they had to move the seats out under the trees. ... Parson Sansom preached in the morning, [[Coltr V.?]] in the evening. Had a splendid dinner on the ground and pretty girls were plenty

subject: Old Mrs [[Liz?]] Hawkins; Old Mr Love; Old man Durst; widow Smith of Johnson Co; Sweet; Jim
statement: Marriages; widow Smith reported to have a hundred negroes; Jim reported gone to the Feds
verbatim_quotation: Last Sunday night Old Mrs [[Liz?]] Hawkins and Old Mr Love were united in the bonds of matrimony; and not long since, Old man Durst and a widow Smith of Johnson Co; It is reported she has a hundred negroes. ... I saw Sweet Sunday, it is reported that Jim has gone to the Feds, but I hardly think he would marry and go right straight off and leave his wife.

subject: Fayette; Jim; George's 24-page letter
statement: Fayette's letters via Henry; men reenlisted 'for 50 years or during the war'; George's letter of 24 pages foolscap giving an account of himself since entering the service
verbatim_quotation: I recd two letters from Fayette yesterday which Henry had recd and sent home. ... the most of them have reenlisted for 50 years or during the war. He says Jim is as lazy as he can be ... He said he had just recd your letter of 24 pages foolscap giving him an acct of yourself since you entered the service; that you had used up Walker and Websters besides using various / "Technical terms"

subject: Baby Sarah; Gale; Mother; sister
statement: Baby (Jesse's daughter) named Sarah by Gale; Mother took her to sister's because of mosquitoes
verbatim_quotation: Mother took the little baby over to sisters nearly a week ago to stay till they disappear some. We will call the baby Sarah. I do not think it is a pretty name, but Gale named her that.

subject: Mary Jeffers; the Colony presbyterian meeting; John Andrews; Adolphus (Delphus)
statement: Meeting continuing; John Andrews and Adolphus home to cut wheat; the little book sent to Ellen
verbatim_quotation: Little Mary Jeffers is the only one that has professed yet ... Big presbyterian meeting commences at the Colony to morrow. John Andrews and Adolphus are at home now got here home to cut wheat. ... We recd yours of the 9th the other day, also the little book to Ellen.

subject: Sue Bell; Lizzie Douglas; George
statement: Slip: to Brother (George) from Sue Bell & Lizzie Douglas, Aug. 19, 1864, Letter no. 16
verbatim_quotation: To Brother (George) / from Sue Bell & Lizzie / Douglas / Aug. 19, 1864 / Letter no. 16

subject: Sue (at Liberty school house); Mr. Rockett; Joda; [[W?]] Jones; Henry; Rome
statement: Sue teaching at Liberty school house; paper sent; Rome hauling cotton below San Antonio for Laredo; promise of hauling to Matamoras
verbatim_quotation: Liberty school house / August [[18th?]] 1864 No 16 ... Mr. Rockett came in this morning, and handed Me a roll of paper which I suppose you must have sent ... [[Sue?]] had just recd a letter from Rome. They were four miles below SanAntonio loaded for Laredo. ... After they get back to San Antonio they have the promise of hauling to Matamoras

subject: Sue; Lizzie Graves; Liberty Spring; Miss Beckett; Sabine fleas
statement: Lizzie Graves the only girl of her age at school; old Liberty Spring; fleas 'as thick as flies down at Sabine'; Parson Justin's wife died
verbatim_quotation: [[illegible]] and Lizzie Graves are the only girls of my age ... the old Liberty Spring. We go there [[illegible]] every day to eat our dinner ... plenty of fleas. They are about as thick as flies down at Sabine ... I heard this morning of the death of Parson Justins wife she died yesterday

subject: Bro Goodwin; spelling match
statement: Bro Goodwin and the boys arranged benches for a spelling match
verbatim_quotation: Bro Goodwin and the boys took down the stove, and moved the benches round generally ... then began the bustle of spelling.

subject: Ann & Cynthia; aunt Catherine; Warren Payne; Preston Payne
statement: Warren Payne dying, youngest child of Preston Payne, taken by aunt Catherine at nine days old; chronic diarrhoea; nearly 17 months
verbatim_quotation: Ann & Cynthia have just passed by going from aunt Catherines and say Warren Payne is dying ... Warren Payne is the youngest child of Preston Payne whom aunt [[inserted: Catherine]] took when he was only nine days old ... His disease was chronic diarhea.

subject: Lynn Norman; Eppa; Sibley's Brigade; Gran Jetter (Jetton); Mr. Chappell; Bob; Ada Chappell; Dock
statement: Lynn Norman home on furlough from the Rio Grande, to report at Sabinetown 8 Sept; Eppa's regiment ordered to Arizona; Gran Jetton digging a well, patriotism cooled; Chappells 'violent secesh'; Dock deserted
verbatim_quotation: Lynn Norman is at home on furlough; he has been out on the RioGrande for some months but is on his way to La. He has to report at Sabinetown on the eighth of Sept. He says the Reg. to which Eppa belongs has been ordered to Arizona. Another wildgoose chase like that of Sibleys Brigade. Gran Jetter is still at home. ... His patriotism has cooled down several degrees below zero. ... Miss Ada Chappell is living at Gran Jettons ... for Dock deserted and went home from La. last fall

subject: Ellen and Laura [[Coffy?]]; Mrs [[Graithwaite?]]; Jennie Bell; uncle Johny; Joe Witherspoon; Mr and Miss Anthony; uncle Joe; Tom Witherspoon
statement: Sat up till two o'clock; Tom Witherspoon home with a hole in his head
verbatim_quotation: Ellen and Laura [[Coffy?]] Mrs [[Graithwaite?]] Jennie Bell and uncle Johny Joe Witherspoon and Mr and Miss Anthony were at uncles Joes. ... Tom Witherspoon is now at home with a hole in his head large enough to put your thumb in, the covering of his brain can be seen.

subject: George Douglas; Walker; Lt. Allen
statement: George's furlough number 13; 'Now that Walker is in command, perhaps more men will be furloughed'; Lt. Allen reported shot on the 5th
verbatim_quotation: I suppose you were so badly disappointed is the reason you said nothing about drawing for a furlough. If it is number 13. I want to know something about when your time will come to get off. ... Now that Walker is in command, perhaps more men will be furloughed. The paper said Lt. Allen was shot on the 5th but as you said nothing about it in yours of the 7th I suppose it is not true.

subject: Ruth ('sisters black girl'); May; Sam; Mr [[Grames?]]; Mr Grounds; Cousin Dock; Ed
statement: Ruth, sister's black girl, hired for two or three months; socks for Cousin Dock by Ed
verbatim_quotation: Mother and Sue have gone to Mr [[Grames?]] Father to Mr Grounds to take some socks to send to Cousin Dock by Ed. Laura did not come home so I am here by myself, except Ruth, sisters black girl whom we have hired for two or three months. I must go down and stay with May to day ... I hope Sam will get your letter at the P O to day

subject: Gail Douglas; Jesse Douglas; Sarah Gale Douglas; Eveline Gale (Manly) Douglas
statement: Slips: Letter no. 9, April 30, 1864: death by childbirth of Gail Douglas, wife of Jesse Douglas; second slip: birth of Jesse's daughter Sarah Gale Douglas and death of her mother Eveline Gale (Manly) Douglas, April 23, 1864
verbatim_quotation: — Tells of the death by / Childbirth of Gail Douglas, / wife of Jesse Douglas. ... AUNT LIZZIE TO UNCLE GEO. IN ARMY / REGARDING BIRTH OF JESSE'S DAUGHTER, / SARAH GALE DOUGLAS, AND DEATH OF HER / MOTHER EVELINE GALE (MANLY) DOUGLAS, / APRIL 23, 1864.

subject: Jeppe; Gail; Mother; Sue; Henry; Hack
statement: Jeppe again a widower; Gail died Saturday 23 [April 1864]; Mother brought the baby home; Jeppe would give it to Sue and Lizzie; 'Jeppe is fated to a life of trouble'; Henry brought Mother home from Hack
verbatim_quotation: I have sad news to communicate this time; Jeppe is again a widower. Gail died last Saturday (23d). Mother got home yesterday and brought the little baby with her. It is the poorest least one I ever saw ... Mother says Jeppe told her he would give it to Sue and me, poor little orphan, we will all do all we can for it. It seems that Jeppe is fated to a life of trouble. Henry brought Mother home, and left all the balance well on Hack.

subject: Bro Jones; Marshall (Methodist preacher, Ark renegade); Parsons Austin and Haynes; Mary Freeman; Mary Gram
statement: Bro Jones preached three sermons; Austin 'honestly differed on a few points'; Jones met Mr. Stone and preached for the soldiers when they left Dallas
verbatim_quotation: Bro Jones preached three very good sermons. ... he is a methodist preacher, and [[inserted: an]] Ark renegade his name is Marshall. Parsons Austin and Haynes were both there. ... Austin made a few remarks after Jones got through ... He did not court controversy or debate, but he honestly differed on a few points. ... Jones says when you all left Dallas, he [[illegible]] Mr. Stone and preached once for you somewhere on the road.

subject: Joda; Fields; Tarrant; Roxana; Mansfield; Sir; Wax.; Bow; Milligan
statement: Joda got transportation (ox train) from Fields to haul to Milligan; things sent by way of Waxahachie
verbatim_quotation: Joda after some difficulty has succeeded in getting transportation. Fields did not like to grant it, but at last consented ... Joda has now gone to Tarrant to have the things brought down Roxana to Mansfield; he said he would get Sir to come by Wax. so we could send your things over. ... We are very sorry he has to take an ox train as it will take so long to get to Milligan; but he could do no better as Fields positively refused to let him have a mule train.

subject: Lizzie Douglas; George Douglas (Galveston)
statement: Slip: Sept. 6, 1864, Letter no. 16, to George Douglas, Galveston; discussion not to hold union church meetings; Fayette & Jim prisoners, entire brigade captured
verbatim_quotation: To George Douglas / Galveston, Texas. / from Sister / Lizzie Douglas / Brushy Creek / Sept. 6, 1864 / Letter no. 16 / — Mentions discussion / not to hold union / Church meetings / in community / — Speaks of Fayette & / Jim (Orr) being / held as prisoners / entire brigade captured

subject: Mr. Collins; Lou; Frances Blair; Thomas
statement: George's letter of 10 Aug and knife by Mr. Collins; letter from Frances Blair; Thomas not yet in the service
verbatim_quotation: Last thursday I went up to the Office, and got yours of 10th ult. also the knife you sent by Mr. Collins ... I also received one from Frances Blair, who by the way is as good at letter writing, as conversation ... Thomas has not yet gone into the service.

subject: Jeppe; Henry (Dr); Daniel H. Willbanks; Sallie Willbanks; Dr. Orr
statement: Jeppe arrived from Hack Creek; Henry lost two patients incl. Daniel H. Willbanks whom Warren knew; Sallie Willbanks married Dr. Orr and they have parted; Jeppe made 130 bushels of corn
verbatim_quotation: Jeppe arrived this evening. He brings no news, left all well on Hack Creek ... Henry has had a gooddeal of practice of late; he has lost two patients, one of them was Daniel H. Willbanks, Warren [[deleted: knows]] [[inserted: knew]] him. Sallie Willbanks married Dr. Orr, and they have parted. / Jeppe gathered his corn before he came down, made a hundred and thirty bushels.

subject: Nancy Hancock (Stout); her brother; Mr. Telly; J. Bell
statement: Sudden deaths of a strange disease; Mr. Telly's arm mortified; J. Bell suffering from his wound, ball working in his shoulder
verbatim_quotation: Nancy Hancock, (Stout that was) was taken sick on Sunday and died on the next wednesday. ... her little brother was taken suddenly, and died [[deleted: illegible]] in two hours ... Mr. Telly — Nancy [[Culphers?]] husband — has been in bad health for a long time: on last Sunday morning a small red spot made its appearance on his arm ... mortification took place and he died on monday. ... J. Bell is now suffering severely from his wound. His shoulder is greatly swelled, and there is a place six inches long, in which he says he can feel the ball working back and forth.

subject: Father; Mr. Martin; old Toby
statement: Father sold old Toby to Mr. Martin for twenty three dollars in specie
verbatim_quotation: Father has sold old Toby to Mr. Martin, for twenty three dollars in specie.

subject: Mr. L. Evans; Sabine; Magruder
statement: Evans left Sabine on the 31st [Aug 1864], seven days on the road; George's furlough not before Feb; 'I am glad old Magruder is gone'
verbatim_quotation: Mr. L. Evans called on us, and left the books you sent, also the letter from Joda. ... says he left Sabine on the 31st thats only seven days on the road. ... Mr Evans says your time will not come before Feb. he also says you could get leave of absence the same as he did. ... I am glad old Magruder is gone.

subject: The little baby (Sarah)
statement: Five months old, weighs nine pounds
verbatim_quotation: The little baby is five months old and weighs nine pounds.

subject: Meetings at Brushy; Parson Hill; Mr. [[Batakers?]]; Bro Jones; Parson Austin; Milton Rawlins; Sarah Selby; Lizzie [[Burnard?]]
statement: Protracted meeting; Methodists appointed a rival meeting; 'It is only the methodists that are so hostile. the presbyterians are not so afraid of the truth'; four united with the church; Bro Jones's sermon on the unity of the church
verbatim_quotation: Every one preaches his own doctrine with all his might, consequently discussion [[inserted: is]] rife. ... so after studying on it awhile they appointed a meeting in Mr. [[Batakers?]] neighborhood embracing the same time! ... The saying of Parson Hill, "now if me and my neighbor dont agree I just let him alone, dont go about him," had sunk deep in their hearts, so union meetings were forgotten. ... It is only the methodists that are so hostile. the presbyterians are not so afraid of the truth. / Bro Jones was [[inserted: the]] only preacher from a distance ... There were no conversions, but four united with the church — Milton Rawlins, his wife, Sarah Selby, and Lizzie [[Burnard?]]. The meeting closed on monday night at which time Bro Jones preached one of the best sermons I ever heard on the unity of the church.

subject: Parson Austin; Bro Goodman
statement: Austin: 'they (the christians) have the bulge on us'; next protracted meeting in October
verbatim_quotation: In his own language he says "I tell my brethren that they (the christians) have the bulge on us and we had better let them alone". ... an other protracted meeting was appointed for the [[deleted: illegible]] beginning friday night before the first Sunday in Oct. Bro Goodman told us several preachers would be there

subject: Parson Austin; Lis. Gibbs; widow Mc Knight; Fayett and Jim; Mary Morgan; Mr. Phipp; Walk Hatter
statement: Austin courting two weeks after his wife's death; Fayett and Jim captured or killed, whole brigade captured; Mary Morgan to marry Mr. Phipp; Walk Hatter a prisoner four months
verbatim_quotation: Parson Austin was [[deleted: illegible]] waiting on Lis. Gibbs last Sunday, and [[gave?]] Saturday night. Dont you think that is right early? his wife has only been dead a little over two weeks. Father has just returned from the widow Mc Knights; he went down to get an auger to bore for water. He brings two items of news; one is that Fayett and Jim have either been taken prisoners or killed. A letter has been recd stating the whole Brigade was captured. ... Mary Morgan is to be married to night to Mr. [[deleted: illegible]] Phipp. ... I saw Walk Hatter the other day ... He was a prisoner four months, and says he fared well while in N's hands. He says the Soldiers he talked with sayed the would fight us ten years but what they would whip us; that old Abe gave them plenty to eat and wear

subject: Lizzie Douglas; George Douglas (Sabine Pass); Mary Andrews; Rob Orr; Norvell Winneford
statement: Slip: Aug. 5, 1864, Letter no 15, to George Douglas, Sabine Pass; party attended by Mary Andrews & Rob Orr; complains of Norvell Winneford working as teamster instead of serving
verbatim_quotation: To George Douglas / Sabine Pass / from / Lizzie Douglas / Brushy Creek / Aug. 5, 1864 / Letter no 15 / — Tells of party attended / by Mary Andrews & / Rob Orr / — Complains of Norvell / Winneford working as / teamster instead of / serving

subject: George Douglas
statement: George [moved] in the Reg.; P. H. married 'while the field was clear'
verbatim_quotation: Though I am sorry to hear through Joda that you have been [[illegible]] in the Reg. You seemed to be getting along so well in the [[illegible]] I almost wished you could remain there. You seem to think P. H's chance of winning a fair one was rather bad, and that he had to marry while the field was clear.

subject: Ed Dickson; uncle Graves; Joe; Laura; Em; Bee; May; Mary Orr; Sue; Bob Andrews
statement: Candy pulling at uncle Graves's; young people named
verbatim_quotation: Ed Dickson. He has got a furlough and is on a visit to this neighborhood now; he came over to invite us to a candy [[pulling?]] at his uncle graves's given in honor [[illegible]] who was to start back to the army Wednesday. ... Laura and Joe went over ... Em's, Bee, May and [[illegible]] were there, [[illegible]] and Mary Orr were the only [[illegible]] ... Sue, Bee, Joe [[illegible]], Bob Andrews Joe and "Ed the genus."

subject: Election, Aug 1864: Frank Hawkins; Motes; Mr Love (Bay's Father, Mal. married); [[Bib?]] Hawkins; [[Tom?]] [[Coltham?]]; [[Norvell?]]; Abb; uncle Jim
statement: Frank Hawkins re-elected clerk; Love 130, Coltham 159; Norvell holds two offices, enrolling officer and general of the militia; a man of 50 enrolled in the militia threatens suit for false imprisonment
verbatim_quotation: last monday was election day. The result is this, Frank Hawkins was elected again for city clerk. His opponents was named Motes Mr Love, (Bay's Father and the same one Mal. married). [[Bib?]] Hawkins, [[Tom?]] [[Coltham?]] and [[Mr?]] [[illegible]] were the candidates for [[Circuit?]] Clerk ... He only came out about a week before the election & got only ninety votes. Love 130, Coltham 159. [[Norvell?]] will now live [[illegible]], but he already holds two offices—enrolling officer, and general of the militia. ... he protested against serving any longer than till he was fifty. He now says, he is going to stay at home till [[illegible]] after him, and then he is going to sue for false imprisonment

subject: Em Gibbs; Bro Goodman; Cedar Hill
statement: 'worship the Lord next Sunday in our dirty clothes' joke; Bro Goodman's literary discourse; Methodist big meeting near Cedar Hill
verbatim_quotation: We agreed that we did not wish to "worship the Lord next Sunday in our dirty clothes" ha ha. ... This morning Mother, Laura and I went over to [[Lis's?]] [[illegible]] Bro Goodman preached [[illegible]] a literary [[illegible]] discourse. ... They have now [[illegible]] at [[illegible]] somewhere near Cedar Hill.

subject: Steel[e]; Kentuckey Town; [[Chisol?]]; the Guardian
statement: Rumour of whipping Steele in Arkansas and capturing two hundred wagons; seven men hung near Kentucky Town
verbatim_quotation: It is rumour / [[lost: torn edge]] here that we have whipt Steel / in Ars and captured two hundd / waggons. Seven men were recent / ly hung near Kentuckey Town / [[lost: torn edge]] one of these named [[Chisol?]]

subject: Robertson; Z. [[Tackett?]]; [[Old?]] man [[Crum?]]; Jeff Davis
statement: Teamsters keeping out of the army: 'got to drive his waggons! getting biger pay than any of us'
verbatim_quotation: [[illegible]] has succeeded in / getting in as a teamster [[illegible]] Z. / [[Tackett?]] has got in to drive one of / R's teams. ... so you see good luck / for Robertson. ... to see Jeff Davis! got to drive / his waggons! getting biger pay / than any of us"!
